item.title: Frattesi turned down Juventus to return to Lazio
item.description: Frattesi turned down Juventus to return to Lazio Davide Frattesi will come up against Juventus this weekend knowing he could have been lining up for the Bianconeri, after turning them down in the summer to rejoin Lazio. According to TuttoMercatoWeb , Juventus made an attempt to bring the midfielder to Turin during the transfer window. The former Inter man instead opted to return to the club where he grew up, taking on a bigger role at the Stadio Olimpico. ROME, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Davide Frattesi of SS Lazio celebrates after scoring an opening goal during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Genoa CFC at Stadio Olimpico on August 30, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) Frattesi chose Lazio over Juventus move That decision gives Juventus-Lazio an extra edge for the 27-year-old, with both sides chasing places near the top of the Serie A table. Since his return, Frattesi has quickly become one of the key figures in the Biancocelesti midfield. He also has a happy history against the Old Lady. As Il Messaggero recalls, Frattesi scored the opening goal of Sassuolo’s 2-1 win in Turin in October 2021, a strike he has since described as one of the most emotional of his career. BOLOGNA, ITALY – AUGUST 24: Davide Frattesi of Lazio looks on before the Serie A match between Bologna FC and SS Lazio at Stadio Renato Dall’Ara on August 24, 2026 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) He will now be looking to hurt Juventus again, this time wearing the shirt of his boyhood club.

item.title: "It would be important to find the path that allows us to string together victories."
item.description: "It would be important to find the path that allows us to string together victories." After completing the last session before the match, Girona FC coach Quique Álvarez has assured that the team arrives with good feelings for tomorrow's duel against Andorra at Montilivi. "The team has trained very well and is eager to play at Montilivi in search of a new victory," explained the coach, who highlighted the importance of finding greater consistency in results. In this regard, he acknowledged that "it would be important to find the rhythm that allows us to string together victories. We have been inconsistent in some aspects, and we need to correct that." Quique Álvarez also focused on the team's ability to manage different moments of the matches. "We need to know how to take advantage of the good moments and manage the bad ones," he stated, convinced that this is one of the key aspects to take a step forward in the competition. Regarding the opponent, the Girona coach warned about the difficulty that Andorra will present. "Andorra is a difficult team to play against. Just recently, they beat Castellón, who had never lost before," he recalled. Even so, he expressed confidence in his players' chances and emphasized that "we will step up and compete for sure." Finally, Quique Álvarez analyzed the recent trajectory of the Andorran team, highlighting their recovery after a more challenging stretch of the season. "Andorra started the league dominating, had a bad streak, but in the last few matches, they have won two games and drawn one," he concluded.

item.title: Marc Bartra talks Pau Cubarsi, Golden Boy award, Raphinha, future Barcelona return: ‘The most decisive team’
item.description: Marc Bartra talks Pau Cubarsi, Golden Boy award, Raphinha, future Barcelona return: ‘The most decisive team’ Former Barcelona defender Marc Bartra has backed Pau Cubarsi to win the Golden Boy award , while describing Hansi Flick’s side as the most decisive attacking team in world football ahead of Real Betis’ meeting with the Catalans. The 35-year-old, who now represents Betis, reflected on Barcelona’s remarkable attacking performances and the development of their young centre-back in an interview with SPORT . Bartra also singled out Raphinha’s extraordinary form and explained what it takes to contain Barcelona’s dangerous forward line. Having experienced Barcelona from inside the dressing room, the former Blaugrana defender offered a detailed assessment of the qualities that make Flick’s team so difficult to stop. Bartra backs Cubarsi to win the Golden Boy award Bartra believes Cubarsi deserves the prestigious individual award because of his performances, consistency and maturity despite his young age. The Barcelona defender has established himself as a regular for both his club and the Spanish national team, something Bartra considers particularly significant for a player in his position. “I’d give it to him. He’s earned it through his performances, and especially the way he conducts himself on the pitch – tactically, technically and in terms of his character – despite his young age. “There are some very good players out there, but he’s a first-team regular at Barcelona and for the Spanish national team, and as far as I’m concerned, he’s the leading contender. “It’s not easy for a defender to be awarded this sort of prize. “When all these factors come together – with this generation of players, getting playing time and consistency – the football inside you can really flourish. Bartra has backed Pau Cubarsi for Golden Boy award. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “It’s unusual to see a player of his age in this position. What he does is hugely valuable. “I always say that I played alongside Gerard Pique, and his situation is very similar to Cubarsi’s. “I haven’t played with Cubarsi, but we’ve faced each other, and who knows, perhaps one day we’ll meet up, whether for the Catalan or Spanish national teams, to learn from one another.” Bartra names Barcelona as the most decisive attacking team Barcelona’s attacking output has been one of the defining features of their campaign, with the Catalans averaging more than four goals per match. item.content:encoded: Marc Bartra talks Pau Cubarsi, Golden Boy award, Raphinha, future Barcelona return: ‘The most decisive team’ Former Barcelona defender Marc Bartra has backed Pau Cubarsi to win the Golden Boy award , while describing Hansi Flick’s side as the most decisive attacking team in world football ahead of Real Betis’ meeting with the Catalans. The 35-year-old, who now represents Betis, reflected on Barcelona’s remarkable attacking performances and the development of their young centre-back in an interview with SPORT . Bartra also singled out Raphinha’s extraordinary form and explained what it takes to contain Barcelona’s dangerous forward line. Having experienced Barcelona from inside the dressing room, the former Blaugrana defender offered a detailed assessment of the qualities that make Flick’s team so difficult to stop. Bartra backs Cubarsi to win the Golden Boy award Bartra believes Cubarsi deserves the prestigious individual award because of his performances, consistency and maturity despite his young age. The Barcelona defender has established himself as a regular for both his club and the Spanish national team, something Bartra considers particularly significant for a player in his position. “I’d give it to him. He’s earned it through his performances, and especially the way he conducts himself on the pitch – tactically, technically and in terms of his character – despite his young age. “There are some very good players out there, but he’s a first-team regular at Barcelona and for the Spanish national team, and as far as I’m concerned, he’s the leading contender. “It’s not easy for a defender to be awarded this sort of prize. “When all these factors come together – with this generation of players, getting playing time and consistency – the football inside you can really flourish. Bartra has backed Pau Cubarsi for Golden Boy award. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “It’s unusual to see a player of his age in this position. What he does is hugely valuable. “I always say that I played alongside Gerard Pique, and his situation is very similar to Cubarsi’s. “I haven’t played with Cubarsi, but we’ve faced each other, and who knows, perhaps one day we’ll meet up, whether for the Catalan or Spanish national teams, to learn from one another.” Bartra names Barcelona as the most decisive attacking team Barcelona’s attacking output has been one of the defining features of their campaign, with the Catalans averaging more than four goals per match. Bartra believes their threat extends beyond individual talent, pointing to their movement, positioning and ability to attack in different situations. “Offensively speaking, Barcelona are currently, in my view, the most decisive team in the world. “Not just because of their physicality and talent, but also because of the way they position themselves in attack, how they find space, and how they attack—whether in set-piece situations or on the counter-attack. “They have a lot of possession, and when they attack, they do so whilst in excellent physical condition. “This allows players like Raphinha, Lamine and Olmo to reach their very best. “To stop them, you need a great deal of communication, leadership and character in defence, because it’s down to everyone, not just the centre-backs. Bartra has praised Barcelona’s performance under Hansi Flick. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “It’s about the team’s behaviour off the ball across all lines, and getting plenty of support: the centre-backs help the full-backs, the midfielders help the centre-backs, and you have to be more intuitive and focused than usual.” Raphinha becoming increasingly difficult to stop Raphinha’s current form has added another angle to Barcelona’s attack, and Bartra believes the Brazilian is operating at a level that makes him particularly difficult for defenders to contain. “At the moment, he seems unstoppable. He’s going through a brilliant spell – an absolutely stunning run. “You might be able to stop him in one moment, but in the next he’ll get past you with ease, using his dribbling and quick shooting. “He’s one of the players most capable of making a difference at the moment.” Bartra opens up on a possible Barcelona return Despite representing Betis, Bartra retains a strong emotional connection with Barcelona, where he developed as a footballer. Asked whether he could return to the Catalan club one day, the defender explained how supporters of both teams continue to make him feel appreciated. “People say that to me a lot on the street – a lot of Betis fans, but also when I go elsewhere, Barcelona fans remember me a lot, and that makes me feel very proud. “ After all, you know what Barcelona means to me. “ And I feel proud when people remember me in Barcelona as well as at Betis, because they’re two clubs I love with all my heart,” he concluded.

item.title: Braves News: Brett Wisely to 40-man roster, Tate Southisene, and more
item.description: The Atlanta Braves have already made some moves this offseason, according to the transaction log. Most notably, infielder Brett Wisely was selected to the major league roster. Outfielder DaShawn Keirsey Jr. was outrighted to Triple-A Gwinnett, and infielder Luke Williams elected free agency. Given his limited big league experience, the decision to add Wisely to the 40-man gives the Braves the option to use him in a later transaction. Atlanta will have plenty of decisions to make as it looks to improve the roster for 2027, and these early moves are a reminder that the team is already working to create flexibility for what comes next. More Braves News: Tate Southisene reached base four times in the recent Arizona Fall League matchup. More in the minor league recap. MLB News: Game 4 of the ALCS has been postponed to tonight due to inclement weather. Game 5 is slated for Sunday evening. From the Feed: Braves special assistant Martin Maldonado is headed to the Detroit Tigers as a quality control coach.

item.title: Eagles’ Jalen Hurts blood clot conspiracy theory recklessly spewed by NFL analyst
item.description: Michael Robinson , an NFL Network analyst, channeling his own version of Charlie’s ‘Pepe Silvia’ rant from “ It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia ,” said Thursday that Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is using a superficial blood clot to escape blame for a losing season. The team’s medical timeline and outside doctors undercut that claim. On “NFL Gameday Kickoff,” Robinson told viewers to “go Google ‘superficial blood clot’ as opposed to a ‘real blood clot.’” He then said Hurts was “ pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” MORE: Concerning Jalen Hurts blood clot note from former NFL team doctor What did Robinson say about Hurts? Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The former Seahawks fullback started by saying the Eagles appeared to be “trying to pin the outcome of this season on Jalen Hurts just so they could have an excuse later on to move on from Jalen Hurts.” He then argued that anyone in Hurts’ camp would respond, “Well, if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt too.” Robinson also picked up former Jaguars running back Maurice Jones-Drew’s phrase “lost season.” He used it to describe the quarterback’s absence as self-preservation. Robinson said “I don’t know anything” several times and added “I’m not a medical guy.” But in the same segment he told the audience to research the diagnosis themselves, so the disclaimers didn’t soften the accusation. The theory feeds off a rough stretch in Philadelphia. The Eagles are 2-3 after three straight losses. Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired abruptly on Oct. 6, and the team traded former Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens a day later. The guaranteed money on Hurts’ five-year, $255 million extension runs out after the 2027 season. How the Eagles found the clot The team’s statement lays out a timeline that doesn’t fit a player looking for an exit. Hurts was cleated in the calf during the Oct. 4 loss to the Rams, practiced in full that week and requested treatment after practice on Oct. 8. An ultrasound in London that Saturday revealed the superficial clot, and doctors there concluded “activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play.” The 28-year-old played every offensive snap in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars, riding a stationary bike between series and completing 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown. A quarterback trying to dodge blame for a losing season had an easy out that weekend and didn’t take it. The NFL also confirmed it communicated with the Eagles about the clot before kickoff in London. A follow-up ultrasound Wednesday night “revealed movement in the small blood clot,” and that finding is what ruled him out. item.content:encoded: Michael Robinson , an NFL Network analyst, channeling his own version of Charlie’s ‘Pepe Silvia’ rant from “ It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia ,” said Thursday that Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is using a superficial blood clot to escape blame for a losing season. The team’s medical timeline and outside doctors undercut that claim. On “NFL Gameday Kickoff,” Robinson told viewers to “go Google ‘superficial blood clot’ as opposed to a ‘real blood clot.’” He then said Hurts was “ pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” MORE: Concerning Jalen Hurts blood clot note from former NFL team doctor What did Robinson say about Hurts? Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The former Seahawks fullback started by saying the Eagles appeared to be “trying to pin the outcome of this season on Jalen Hurts just so they could have an excuse later on to move on from Jalen Hurts.” He then argued that anyone in Hurts’ camp would respond, “Well, if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt too.” Robinson also picked up former Jaguars running back Maurice Jones-Drew’s phrase “lost season.” He used it to describe the quarterback’s absence as self-preservation. Robinson said “I don’t know anything” several times and added “I’m not a medical guy.” But in the same segment he told the audience to research the diagnosis themselves, so the disclaimers didn’t soften the accusation. The theory feeds off a rough stretch in Philadelphia. The Eagles are 2-3 after three straight losses. Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired abruptly on Oct. 6, and the team traded former Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens a day later. The guaranteed money on Hurts’ five-year, $255 million extension runs out after the 2027 season. How the Eagles found the clot The team’s statement lays out a timeline that doesn’t fit a player looking for an exit. Hurts was cleated in the calf during the Oct. 4 loss to the Rams, practiced in full that week and requested treatment after practice on Oct. 8. An ultrasound in London that Saturday revealed the superficial clot, and doctors there concluded “activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play.” The 28-year-old played every offensive snap in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars, riding a stationary bike between series and completing 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown. A quarterback trying to dodge blame for a losing season had an easy out that weekend and didn’t take it. The NFL also confirmed it communicated with the Eagles about the clot before kickoff in London. A follow-up ultrasound Wednesday night “revealed movement in the small blood clot,” and that finding is what ruled him out. Left tackle Jordan Mailata said Hurts “persevered to play in that game for us.” MORE: Handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot will prove to be defining moment for Eagles Why doctors take the clot seriously The word “movement” is what worries former Chargers team doctor David Chao . Chao said a superficial clot can move and stay superficial. A clot that reaches a deep vein is a different situation. “If it’s a deep vein thrombosis, it starts to be measured in months, not weeks,” Chao said. If a deep vein clot breaks loose and reaches the lungs, it becomes a pulmonary embolism, which Chao said would end Hurts’ season. The strong anticoagulants used to treat it also carry bleeding risks. Chao said, “The big fear is, what if you have a brain bleed?” Temple Health vascular surgeon Andrea Lubitz said superficial clots are generally treated with compresses and painkillers, though some patients need more extensive care. The Eagles’ statement says the team is still determining “the appropriate course of treatment.” Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott called the situation “scary.” He added that “you’re talking about someone’s life, especially with the plane trip.” The Eagles haven’t set a timetable for the Super Bowl 59 MVP’s return. Tanner McKee will start Sunday when the Panthers visit Lincoln Financial Field. item.title: Saquon Barkley Injury Update: Eagles RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed
item.description: Saquon Barkley is battling a hamstring injury originally suffered against the Los Angeles Rams, and he will not play in Week 6. Originally entering the league as the second-overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft , the Penn State product hit the ground running, recording 1,307 yards and 11 touchdowns as a rookie for the New York Giants. He remained an elite running back during his five years with the club before joining the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, where he immediately led the league with 2,005 rushing yards while playing a key role in the team’s championship run. Through four games, Saquon Barkley has recorded a decent 182 yards and no touchdowns on 36 attempts. However, he won’t add to those numbers against the Carolina Panthers. Barkley suffered a hamstring injury during Week 4, and ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the team has officially ruled him out for Week 6. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor Saquon Barkley Injury Update: Eagles RB Didn’t Practice Wednesday The Last Word The Philadelphia Eagles are always at their best with Saquon Barkley in the lineup, but the team desperately needs him to return sooner rather than later. Backup running back Tank Bigsby is currently on the injured reserve, and third-string running back Will Shipley suffered a foot injury that could sideline him for weeks. Quite frankly, the Eagles are running out of bodies at the running back position. With Saquon Barkley sidelined, the team will likely turn to former Houston Texans running back Dameon Pierce to lead the backfield. A former fourth-round pick himself, the Florida product had a promising rookie season in 2022, finishing the campaign with 939 yards and four touchdowns on 220 attempts. However, it’s been all downhill for him since that date. The running back made his debut for the Eagles last week and finished with just 14 rushing yards on 11 attempts.

item.title: Sonay Kartal makes history by reaching biggest final of her career in Wuhan
item.description: Great Britain’s Sonay Kartal made WTA history as she defeated Jelena Ostapenko to reach the biggest final of her career at the Wuhan Open in China. Kartal began the tournament ranked No 170 in the world having missed six months of the season due to a back injury, but has made up for lost time superbly in what is just her second tour-level tournament since March. The 24-year-old has become the lowest-ranked WTA 1000 finalist since the format was introduced in 2009, with victory over former French Open champion Ostapenko adding to impressive wins against world No 6 Elina Svitolina , former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic and former Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini this week. It took another gutsy display from Kartal, who trailed in both sets against the big-hitting Ostapenko but prevailed in a rollercoaster encounter to win two tiebreaks 7-6 (11-9), 7-6 (7-5), saving all six set points she faced across the two-hour battle. Kartal, whose only career title came in the WTA 250 event in Monastir two years ago, will play either six-time grand slam champion Iga Swiatek or French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska in Sunday’s final, with the all-Polish semi-final taking place later on Saturday. “Wow! That was probably one of the toughest of matches I've played,” Kartal said after converting her second match point. “I knew exactly how she was gonna play. At times, she's unplayable, and sometimes you just have to ride that wave. “Mentally, I think this is one of the best performances I've had in my career, so, I’m very, very proud of that one.” More follows

item.title: England stunned by Tonga in World Cup opener
item.description: Tonga had lost their previous six meetings with England before triumphing here [Getty Images] England (0) 12 Try : Brimson, Young Goal : Savala 2 Tonga (10) 30 Tries : Olakau'atu 2, Utoikamanu, Koula Goals : Katoa 3 Penalties : Katoa 4 Four years ago, England were left shocked and shattered by Samoa in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals. Now in 2026, Tonga - another Pacific island nation - have done the same with a victory to put England's Australian campaign in immediate jeopardy. Tonga combined classy attacking play with staunch defence, mixed with a pinch of luck - while being cheered on by a ferociously partisan crowd in Perth - to cause a major upset. It was expected that Brian McDermott's team - ranked third in the world - would have enough to open their Group B-C campaign with victory over opponents ranked fifth. But they will now have to pick themselves up for coming group games against France and Papua New Guinea to try to secure a top-two finish in the combined six-team group table and secure a semi-final spot. England's day came apart amid seemingly endless mistakes, wastefulness and a few dodgy refereeing decisions. Arguably the turning point came on 22 minutes, when England got to within a few yards of the opposition line but Victor Radley knocked on after an absolute boneshaker from Tonga captain Jason Taumalolo. The ball was turned over, and the Tongans scored two minutes later. Stefano Utoikamanu streaked through after Isaiya Katoa's superb inside pass cut out George Williams and Kai Pearce-Paul, to the delight of the massed Tongan fans in Perth. For England, it seemed as if the universe was against them. The impressive Katoa converted two penalties given following debatable calls. First, Harry Smith was penalised for obstruction when Dallin Watene-Zelezniak ran into him. Then, Herbie Farnworth conceded a sloppy penalty on the verge of half-time when accidentally tripping Watene-Zelezniak off the ball. England badly needed half-time, and they came out refreshed. Their first flowing move of the home game led to a try for full-back AJ Brimson after being set up by a sensational driving run from Young, holding off two tacklers over 20 metres. Waves of England attacks began to crash on the Tongan defence, but Tonga stood firm and benefited from a moment of fortune as Haumole Olakau'atu pounced after his sketchy first grubber kick was kicked on behind the England line. And with England wobbling, Tonga landed a one-two punch when Tolutau Koula drove over the line. Young went over in the corner to give England false hope, but in front of their delirious fans Tonga scored their fourth try as Katoa's grubber kick exploited defensive gaps for Olakau'atu to touch down. In the day's other men's game - also in Group B-C - co-hosts Papua New Guinea defeated Lebanon 42-18.

item.title: Mike Evans’ Friday Absence Signals Real Risk For 49ers Offense
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Mike Evans missed his second straight practice on Friday while dealing with ribs and Achilles soreness. Harrison Rich of The San Francisco Chronicle reported he is listed as a non-participant. The 33-year-old star is now questionable for Monday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. His absence creates a massive void in the passing game right when the team needs him most. The 49ers simply cannot afford to lose their best pass-catcher to the Injured Reserve list this year. Evans has not played all week, but the team is holding him back to avoid a longer absence. If he returns to the field on Saturday, his chances of playing on Monday improve significantly. This is a classic case of managing a veteran’s body to keep him on the field for the big game. The Injury Math Does Not Look Good Evans is fighting two different injuries at the same time. He has been battling a painful rib injury and is now dealing with soreness in his Achilles. These are two of the worst spots for a wide receiver to get hurt. Ribs make it hard to catch and block. Achilles issues destroy speed and cutting ability. The combination makes it very hard to trust he can go full speed on Monday. According to reports, the 49ers are trying to balance his health with the need to win. The team knows that missing practice is not ideal, but they are prioritizing his long-term availability. So far this season, Evans has captured 24 of his 34 targets, totaling 326 yards and three touchdowns. Those numbers show he is still a dominant force even while hurt. Losing those production numbers for even one game would hurt the offense badly. Deebo Samuel’s Absence Makes It Worse The timing of this injury is terrible because Deebo Samuel Sr. is also out. Samuel is expected to miss time due to a hamstring injury he suffered during the Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. This leaves the 49ers with a very thin group of healthy receivers. With Samuel out, Evans will see an even higher target share if active. The defense will focus entirely on him if he plays, or on the backup options if he does not. According to RotoBaller NFL , Evans remains a must-start WR2 in fantasy football despite these nagging injuries. His ability to produce while hurt shows his toughness. But toughness has limits. This season, the 49ers cannot afford for their best pass-catcher to join the list of wideouts on Injured Reserve. Consequently, he has not been practicing much during the week. The risk of playing too soon is too high. What Saturday Practice Means The final practice session of the week on Saturday will tell us everything. A return to practice on Saturday could give Evans a good chance of playing in Week 6. This is the key moment for fans and fantasy managers to watch. The team needs to see him move without pain before they clear him for the game. The 49ers are in a tough spot with their roster depth and injury list. item.title: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes already hang by a thread after brutal Tonga defeat
item.description: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes are hanging by a thread after a crushing 30-12 defeat by Tonga in their opening match of the competition in Perth. Brian McDermott’s men were undone by the brilliance of Dolphins half-back Isaiya Katoa who masterminded his side’s stunning win and contributed a crucial 14 points with the boot. It means England realistically now need Tonga to beat Samoa in a fortnight’s time to stand the slimmest chance of progressing to the semi-final stage. England failed to capitalise on some serious first-half momentum and the Tongans exposed their weaknesses after the break to gain emphatic revenge for their trio of test defeats in the UK in 2023. England’s flat pack were comprehensively out-muscled and full-back AJ Brimson – preferred to St Helens number one Jack Welsby – was turned inside out by Katoa, who will team up with England captain George Williams at his NRL club next season. For McDermott it was a massive wake-up call and he must now rebuild his shattered side for upcoming group games against Papua New Guinea and France, both of which are already in danger of being rendered irrelevant in the complicated cross-group system. England piled on the pressure for much of a high-octane first half but they failed to find a way through an heroic Tongan rearguard and it was the South Sea islanders who reached the interval 10-0 in front. Kai Pearce Paul was denied an early opener by a superb saving tackle from Latu Fainu, and Brimson was hauled back by Lehi Hopoate, and Tonga suffered a major blow when playmaker Fainu was forced off injured. But after soaking up half an hour of pressure, Tonga pounced when Katoa’s inch-perfect offload sent Stefano Utoikamanu galloping over for their opener. Tonga would stretch their lead into double figures through two kicks from Katoa, but McDermott’s men looked to have forced their way right back into the contest when Hugo Savala sent Brimson over within six minutes of the restart. Savala’s subsequent kick took England within four and they looked to have all the momentum until a needless penalty sent Tonga back up the other end of the field and they seized on a slice of fortune when Katoa’s kick ricocheted through and Haumole Olakau’atu touched down. It got much worse for England as a clever kick through by former Huddersfield man Tui Lolohea sent Tolutau Koula over for his side’s third. Katoa’s sixth successful kick stretched Tonga’s lead to 18 as the game edged beyond the hour mark. Dom Young gave England hope when he raced over on 63 minutes, but it was to prove a fleeting moment of hope as another Katoa kick sent Olakau’atu sent over for his second, and Tonga cruised through the final minutes to wrap up a richly deserved win. More follows

item.title: Celtics' Unusual Win Over 76ers Leaves Joe Mazzulla With Intriguing Decisions
item.description: Celtics' Unusual Win Over 76ers Leaves Joe Mazzulla With Intriguing Decisions originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics probably could not have designed a more unusual way to finish their preseason. Facing a Philadelphia 76ers team featuring Joel Embiid, LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey and former Celtics star Jaylen Brown, Boston decided to give its regular contributors the night off. Instead of using a conventional starting lineup, the Celtics opened with Chris Cenac Jr., Milos Uzan, Hayden Gray, Tucker DeVries and Gabe McGlothan. The result was a 125-120 overtime victory that gave Boston a perfect 4-0 preseason record. That final score is entertaining enough. But what happened during the game might be even more interesting for Joe Mazzulla and the Celtics' coaching staff. Boston's reserves did not simply survive against a more recognizable Philadelphia lineup. They found a way to win after falling behind late. For a team preparing to open the regular season, that is a pretty encouraging problem to have. MORE : Celtics Overcome Massive Depth Disadvantage to Beat 76ers in Preseason Finale Celtics Reserves Refuse To Follow The Script The 76ers had the recognizable names and the established star power. Boston had players competing for opportunities, developmental minutes and potentially roster positions. On paper, that looked like a difficult matchup for the Celtics. 4-0 preseason ✅ https://t.co/o0equnOnrl — Boston Celtics (@celtics) October 17, 2026 Philadelphia built a 10-point advantage in the fourth quarter, putting Boston in a position where a preseason loss would hardly have been surprising. Instead, the Celtics fought back and forced overtime before completing the victory. Hugo Gonzalez led Boston with 21 points, continuing to demonstrate why his development is worth watching. item.content:encoded: Celtics' Unusual Win Over 76ers Leaves Joe Mazzulla With Intriguing Decisions originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics probably could not have designed a more unusual way to finish their preseason. Facing a Philadelphia 76ers team featuring Joel Embiid, LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey and former Celtics star Jaylen Brown, Boston decided to give its regular contributors the night off. Instead of using a conventional starting lineup, the Celtics opened with Chris Cenac Jr., Milos Uzan, Hayden Gray, Tucker DeVries and Gabe McGlothan. The result was a 125-120 overtime victory that gave Boston a perfect 4-0 preseason record. That final score is entertaining enough. But what happened during the game might be even more interesting for Joe Mazzulla and the Celtics' coaching staff. Boston's reserves did not simply survive against a more recognizable Philadelphia lineup. They found a way to win after falling behind late. For a team preparing to open the regular season, that is a pretty encouraging problem to have. MORE : Celtics Overcome Massive Depth Disadvantage to Beat 76ers in Preseason Finale Celtics Reserves Refuse To Follow The Script The 76ers had the recognizable names and the established star power. Boston had players competing for opportunities, developmental minutes and potentially roster positions. On paper, that looked like a difficult matchup for the Celtics. 4-0 preseason ✅ https://t.co/o0equnOnrl — Boston Celtics (@celtics) October 17, 2026 Philadelphia built a 10-point advantage in the fourth quarter, putting Boston in a position where a preseason loss would hardly have been surprising. Instead, the Celtics fought back and forced overtime before completing the victory. Hugo Gonzalez led Boston with 21 points, continuing to demonstrate why his development is worth watching. Tucker DeVries, Ron Harper Jr. and Dillon Mitchell also provided important contributions as the Celtics worked their way back into the game. The performance did not guarantee anybody additional regular-season minutes. Preseason basketball does not work that way. However, the effort gave Boston's coaching staff another opportunity to evaluate players in situations that cannot be completely replicated during practice. Late-game possessions, defensive assignments and decision-making under pressure all provide useful information. The Celtics received plenty of it Friday. More Celtics Latest Celtics news TD Garden fan guide: What to know before you go Complete history of Celtics championships Sam Cassell Gets An Interesting Assignment Another unusual aspect of the evening involved the coaching staff. Mazzulla handed the sideline responsibilities to assistant coach Sam Cassell, continuing Boston's approach of allowing assistants to gain valuable experience during preseason games. Cassell was tasked with managing a lineup that looked considerably different from the one Boston expects to use during the regular season. That created opportunities for evaluation beyond the players themselves. Coaches must determine which combinations work together, which players understand defensive responsibilities and who can execute when the game becomes competitive. Friday offered an opportunity to make those assessments without the pressure of regular-season standings. Cassell's group responded with a victory. The result also reflected something that has become an important part of Boston's preseason identity: defensive activity and a willingness to compete regardless of the personnel on the floor. Those qualities will matter when the Celtics begin playing games that count. MORE: Celtics’ Joe Mazzulla Snubbed in GM Survey Despite Reigning COTY Status Boston's Real Decisions Begin Now The Celtics open their regular season Tuesday, October 20, against the Detroit Pistons. At that point, the focus will shift from experimentation to winning games. Jayson Tatum, Derrick White and Boston's other established contributors will command significant minutes. Opportunities for players farther down the roster will become more limited. That is why Friday's performance was meaningful. The coaching staff received another look at several players who may not have many chances to demonstrate their value once the regular season begins. Gonzalez's scoring performance was encouraging. The contributions from Boston's younger players were also worth noting. But the most impressive aspect of the victory might have been the collective response. The Celtics could have accepted a preseason loss against a Philadelphia team featuring several accomplished veterans. Instead, they continued competing and found a way to win. An undefeated preseason does not guarantee anything once the regular season begins. Boston knows that. What it does provide is evidence that the team's younger players are willing to compete, even when the matchup looks unfavorable. That should make the final roster evaluations considerably more interesting. And for Mazzulla, having too many players eager to prove they belong is a problem most coaches would gladly accept. item.title: Lions fans’ confidence on the rise; anticipate immediate impact from Brian Branch
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 4: Brian Branch #32 of the Detroit Lions stretches prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 04, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , and asked Detroit Lions fans two questions : Which Lions player returning from injury will have the biggest immediate impact? (weekly question) Are you confident the Lions are headed in the right direction? (recurring poll) Our weekly confidence polls have been a roller coaster ride throughout 2026. After entering the season on a high note, things dipped after they needed overtime to beat the Saints in Week 1, then fell below 50% for the first time in the Dan Campbell era after a bad Week 2 loss in Buffalo. After a Week 3 win over the Jets, confidence rebounded to nearly 80%, only to plummet to 12% the following week after a loss in Carolina. Now, after their third victory of the season, this time over the Cardinals, fans’ confidence in the team has rebounded again, though not quite to where it was before. Let’s take a look at the results of this week’s polls: As for our second question, there was a clear winner, as anticipated, but we wanted to give readers a chance to also comment and share their view on the potential impact of two key players returning from injury. But before we get to that, let’s take a look at the results from this survey: Let’s take a closer look at the comment section of our original article and The Feed post to see fans’ explanations for why they voted the way they did (lightly edited for clarity). Most approved/interacted with “right direction” comments: No Username : “Since a “yes” answer implies full confidence, I’ll stay with “no” until I see some consistency in the defense, and steady performance against better teams.“ Matt48912 : “I answered “no” because I am not confident right now, but I still think they might be. I need more than 3 quarters against a team struggling more than them on defense before I think they are getting back to where they were 2 years ago.” icd8u2 : “Once we acquire another good CB, then I will be fairly confident we are headed in the right direction. No matter what you think of Arnold, losing your first-round CB pick for nothing in return really hurt our CB room.” rbelieve : “I hope they’re headed in the right direction. But I am not “confident”. critical perspective : “I keep reminding myself that there isn’t a team out there who is firing on all cylinders in every aspect of their roster. […] The Lions have an elite offense and a much improved defensive front. The LBs and, to a great extent, defensive backs have struggled, and there just may not be a fix at corner for this season. But overall, there is so much talent on this team that you’d hope they can plug some holes and keep it rolling to at least be in the conversation come January

item.title: Ex-Dolphins Pro Bowl guard shares honest Malik Willis assessment amid 0-5 start
item.description: The Dolphins entered their bye week 0-5 while carrying an NFL-record $182.29 million in dead cap, 60.5% of their total cap. Releasing Tua Tagovailoa accounts for $99.2 million of it, with Tyreek Hill’s release and the Jaylen Waddle trade to Denver adding most of the rest. Several early 2027 mock drafts already have Miami using the first overall pick on a quarterback to eventually replace Malik Willis. Willis signed a three-year, $67.5 million deal with $45 million guaranteed this offseason. Richie Incognito, the former Dolphins guard who now co-hosts the Initial Contact podcast with former NFL tight end Christian Fauria, weighed in on that plan in an interview with Covers.com. Dec 27, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Malik Willis (2) warms up prior to the game against the Baltimore Ravens at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images “I think they got to get the rest of the team right. You’ve got to get a real serious offensive line. You’ve got to get some receivers on the edge that will threaten a defense or make things easier for a quarterback. They need so many more upgrades. So just throwing a quarterback into the mix, I don’t think it fixes their problem.” Incognito told Covers.com . Willis has completed 56.2% of his passes for 849 yards and two touchdowns, all of which rank last among starting quarterbacks , with four interceptions. His top pass catchers are Malik Washington and first-year players Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and De’Von Achane is out for the year with a torn ACL. The numbers belong to Willis, but the names around him explain a good share of them. “It’s tough to really pass judgment on Malik Willis because it’s up and down. I think the rest of the roster is really, really bad. They’re paying $180 million to guys that are no longer there. Overall, they’re just not a very good football team. There’s a lot of holes in the roster. Maybe they make a change at quarterback. It doesn’t matter.” Incognito said. Head coach Jeff Hafley has stuck with Willis through all five losses. “We’ve played five games and Malik is our quarterback. We need to be better. Malik needs to be better, OK? And that’s not the headline.” Hafley said Monday. Can the Dolphins avoid a winless season? Miami’s last two losses came by five points at Minnesota and seven at home against Cincinnati. The Dolphins return Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET at the 2-3 Jets, the first of two meetings with New York. The Chargers, also 0-5, visit Hard Rock Stadium on Dec. 27. Those three games come against opponents with a combined 2-8 record. Green Bay Packers quarterback Malik Willis (2) throws during the third quarter of their game against the Baltimore Ravens Saturday, December 27, 2025 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. “I could see them getting a win somewhere along the way. item.title: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Militao, Guler, Valverde ahead of Real Madrid vs Sevilla
item.description: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Militao, Guler, Valverde ahead of Real Madrid vs Sevilla Real Madrid once again had to fight against all odds to get a win when they travelled to the Italian capital to face AS Roma in their second UEFA Champions League game of the season. After going down 3-1 at one point in game, the Merengues fought their way back to a 3-4 win in the final few minutes of the match. This win would have significantly boosted the team’s morale, and there is plenty of reason for Los Blancos’ fans to hope that their performance in that game will help the team turn around their form. However, they face another difficult test, this time in La Liga, as they will host Sevilla on Sunday. As MARCA has reported, Jose Mourinho addressed his customary press conference ahead of this league match. The Portuguese coach admitted that some of his players are tired, but assured that they will be ready for the upcoming game: “We are tired, but not tomorrow. From what I’ve seen in the medical department, the players who played the most minutes are tired. Tomorrow is another day. We have good options at home to make some changes and bring in fresh legs. Sevilla are doing well, and they have been competitive in the matches they have lost. Luis García is doing a great job. They survived last season. We want to win.” The midfield been one of the main areas of problem for Real Madrid, and the coach was asked about his plans for this position: “I ask midfielders to be midfielders. I expect them to do the work a midfielder is supposed to do. Someone who only defends is limited. If they only attack, they would be better off playing out wide or as a No. 10. It is a very difficult position to play. To be a top player, you need a different level of quality.” Mourinho was highly criticial of Javier Tebas after his recent comments comparing Real Madrid TV to Nazi propaganda machines: “You’ve already seen what I think. He has ventured into an area where the only excuse would be a clinical condition. Madrid fans understand what Real Madrid are up against. Even considering the enormous prestige Spanish football enjoys abroad, the World Cup and the most prestigious club in the world, it is better that he keeps those comments to himself.” While praising Arda Guler, the Merengue coach did not reveal what position he is planning to play him in: “There is work being done. You find it difficult to give credit for the work. It seems that the more negative things have someone to blame, while the positive things are attributed to failure or luck. Arda is a very talented player; we know that. Obviously, he is not yet a finished product because he is 21. He has the attributes to play in several roles. item.content:encoded: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Militao, Guler, Valverde ahead of Real Madrid vs Sevilla Real Madrid once again had to fight against all odds to get a win when they travelled to the Italian capital to face AS Roma in their second UEFA Champions League game of the season. After going down 3-1 at one point in game, the Merengues fought their way back to a 3-4 win in the final few minutes of the match. This win would have significantly boosted the team’s morale, and there is plenty of reason for Los Blancos’ fans to hope that their performance in that game will help the team turn around their form. However, they face another difficult test, this time in La Liga, as they will host Sevilla on Sunday. As MARCA has reported, Jose Mourinho addressed his customary press conference ahead of this league match. The Portuguese coach admitted that some of his players are tired, but assured that they will be ready for the upcoming game: “We are tired, but not tomorrow. From what I’ve seen in the medical department, the players who played the most minutes are tired. Tomorrow is another day. We have good options at home to make some changes and bring in fresh legs. Sevilla are doing well, and they have been competitive in the matches they have lost. Luis García is doing a great job. They survived last season. We want to win.” The midfield been one of the main areas of problem for Real Madrid, and the coach was asked about his plans for this position: “I ask midfielders to be midfielders. I expect them to do the work a midfielder is supposed to do. Someone who only defends is limited. If they only attack, they would be better off playing out wide or as a No. 10. It is a very difficult position to play. To be a top player, you need a different level of quality.” Mourinho was highly criticial of Javier Tebas after his recent comments comparing Real Madrid TV to Nazi propaganda machines: “You’ve already seen what I think. He has ventured into an area where the only excuse would be a clinical condition. Madrid fans understand what Real Madrid are up against. Even considering the enormous prestige Spanish football enjoys abroad, the World Cup and the most prestigious club in the world, it is better that he keeps those comments to himself.” While praising Arda Guler, the Merengue coach did not reveal what position he is planning to play him in: “There is work being done. You find it difficult to give credit for the work. It seems that the more negative things have someone to blame, while the positive things are attributed to failure or luck. Arda is a very talented player; we know that. Obviously, he is not yet a finished product because he is 21. He has the attributes to play in several roles. I’m very happy with him.” The Portuguese tactician talked at some length about Vinicius Junior: “Let me ask you a question. Are your followers interested in what time we arrive at Valdebebas? Are people interested in that? And what about when we leave? It’s funny.” “Vinícius had a very difficult match. Gasperini was primarily responsible for that because he attacked us down just one flank, with three men against Cucurella and him. It is difficult to make changes as a manager when some of the information doesn’t come through properly. What annoyed me was the nature of the second goal, which came at a time when the match had settled down and was balanced. We knew how they pressed man-to-man, and Vini needed to protect the ball or win a foul in that situation. But that’s that. Nothing happened. I made five substitutions; it’s part of football. The intensity is extremely high, and it is difficult to play at 200 kilometres per hour for 90 minutes. “Vini’s future lies in working harder than those who get to play every match. Without making any promises, I think he will start on Wednesday in the Champions League. As for the four-match suspension, I’m happy because I thought he would receive a longer ban. I thought those hidden agendas would get him another one or two matches. We won’t discuss it any further.” Further commenting on the Brazilian forward, Mourinho assured that he is a very good individual to work with: “He is a spectacular young man, and it is very easy to have a good relationship with him. I like him a lot; he is fantastic. He has tremendous strength because he manages to live and survive with a smile on his face. If I were in his position, I probably wouldn’t still be here. This past summer, I would have forced a move to a country or a group of clubs and opponents where I would be respected. Out of love for the club and the city, and because he believes things can improve, he renewed his contract and continues to smile. People can affect him negatively because he is human, but I don’t think anyone will be able to take that joy away from him.” The Real Madrid coach also shared his thoughts on meritocracy in his team and rued that he cannot play all the players: “I think we sometimes struggle to give credit to people who do things well. You hammer them when things go wrong. The credit belongs to the young lad who came on and gave everything. Look at the three goals from corners and how we won those corners. In 10 minutes, we had around seven corners because we were overwhelming them with our football. “There are many players who deserve to play. More than 11 deserve to play — there are 15 or 16. Lunin deserves to play, and I’m not joking. He works every day alongside the best goalkeeper in the world, stays positive, and still doesn’t play. I can’t put both of them on the pitch. It is the same story with outfield players. “We can all agree that the five players who came on and changed the match deserve to play tomorrow. But what about the others? Doesn’t Diomande deserve to play? Doesn’t Cucurella deserve to play? Doesn’t Valverde deserve to play? Doesn’t Mbappé deserve to play? That is what makes a manager’s job difficult. My colleagues who manage teams with fewer resources will say I’m lucky. It is both a blessing and a curse to have journalists like you, who make things more complicated.” The Portuguese coach also shared some good news and assured that he does not want any new players: “Militão will be in the squad tomorrow. The good thing is that I don’t have to name the squad just yet. I’m not asking for signings; I’m happy. The players are improving, especially when we have time and peace. I have to develop them. I’m not in a position to ask for more players. I like having a small squad. For someone to come in, someone would have to leave. If the club’s management considers making a move, we will assess it, but I’m not taking the initiative to ask for players. I’m not asking for one or two signings.” When once again asked about Vinicius, Mourinho refused to reveal what he has told the player: “Those are private conversations. When I arrived, he renewed his contract and signed because he considers Madrid his home. He was excited about continuing to make history and win trophies. He gets along with everyone in the dressing room and brings a lot of joy. I have serious doubts that I would have had the strength to stay here with all the offers he had.” The Real Madrid coach also kept his cards close to his chest when asked about the positions of Guler and Valverde: “I’m here to do what I believe is best for the team. The day will come when polls or artificial intelligence pick the teams and managers are limited to working on the pitch. For now, we are still the ones who select the teams. “I’m not talking about criticism or opinions; I don’t consider those opinions more valuable than the manager’s. A manager who is not open-minded is limited. At the same time, I believe a manager who simply follows polls and opinions is not really a manager. I’m not stubborn. I’m open to the opinions of my staff and to analysis. Can I change my mind? Yes, but I can do so based on my own analysis and work. I always want to improve. A match lasts 90 minutes and has m

item.title: Liverpool made €50m offer to sign Serie A forward
item.description: Liverpool made €50m offer to sign Serie A forward Liverpool Transfer News: Francisco Conceicao Bid Highlights Right-Wing Uncertainty Liverpool’s reported pursuit of Francisco Conceicao has opened up another line of scrutiny around the club’s planning on the right flank. According to TuttoMercato , Liverpool saw a €50m proposal turned down, with Juventus and the player both declining the move. That detail matters. When a club of Liverpool’s scale reaches that level financially and still cannot advance discussions, it tends to suggest interest was not matched by conviction on all sides. In this case, the report points to a deal that never gained the necessary alignment, despite the size of the offer. Francisco Conceicao Interest Underlines Liverpool Recruitment Concerns Conceicao has long been regarded as a technically sharp wide option, capable of carrying the ball and attacking defenders in one-v-one situations. Even so, the wider context is difficult to ignore. Liverpool spent much of the market assessing right-sided attackers and, by the end of it, still had no clear addition in that area. The same broad pattern was seen with other names linked during the window, including Ismaila Sarr, Yankuba Minteh and Ibrahim Mbaye. Yan Diomande was also described as a leading objective earlier in the summer. None of those moves materialised, which leaves the impression of a search that remained active but inconclusive. Photo: IMAGO Right-Wing Replacement Debate Continues The central issue is less about one individual target and more about what the sequence says regarding Liverpool’s market strategy. A reported €50m offer for a player who scored three Serie A goals last season would naturally prompt debate, especially in the context of replacing a major attacking departure. Liverpool’s squad construction has also become part of that discussion. The imbalance referenced by many observers, with several options more comfortable from the left and none regarded as a natural senior answer on the right, has lingered beyond the close of the window. If the Conceicao report is accurate, it reinforces the sense that Liverpool were willing to move decisively for a solution, but without landing one. That leaves the club facing familiar questions about recruitment clarity, role definition and whether the right-wing position was addressed with enough certainty when it mattered most. Our View From a Liverpool perspective, this is one of those reports that feels plausible enough to be uncomfortable. If the club really did put €50m on the table for Conceicao, then it suggests there was genuine anxiety late in the process. That does not automatically mean he is a poor player, far from it, but it does hint at a market where Liverpool were reacting rather than dictating. The biggest concern is the profile of the search. item.content:encoded: Liverpool made €50m offer to sign Serie A forward Liverpool Transfer News: Francisco Conceicao Bid Highlights Right-Wing Uncertainty Liverpool’s reported pursuit of Francisco Conceicao has opened up another line of scrutiny around the club’s planning on the right flank. According to TuttoMercato , Liverpool saw a €50m proposal turned down, with Juventus and the player both declining the move. That detail matters. When a club of Liverpool’s scale reaches that level financially and still cannot advance discussions, it tends to suggest interest was not matched by conviction on all sides. In this case, the report points to a deal that never gained the necessary alignment, despite the size of the offer. Francisco Conceicao Interest Underlines Liverpool Recruitment Concerns Conceicao has long been regarded as a technically sharp wide option, capable of carrying the ball and attacking defenders in one-v-one situations. Even so, the wider context is difficult to ignore. Liverpool spent much of the market assessing right-sided attackers and, by the end of it, still had no clear addition in that area. The same broad pattern was seen with other names linked during the window, including Ismaila Sarr, Yankuba Minteh and Ibrahim Mbaye. Yan Diomande was also described as a leading objective earlier in the summer. None of those moves materialised, which leaves the impression of a search that remained active but inconclusive. Photo: IMAGO Right-Wing Replacement Debate Continues The central issue is less about one individual target and more about what the sequence says regarding Liverpool’s market strategy. A reported €50m offer for a player who scored three Serie A goals last season would naturally prompt debate, especially in the context of replacing a major attacking departure. Liverpool’s squad construction has also become part of that discussion. The imbalance referenced by many observers, with several options more comfortable from the left and none regarded as a natural senior answer on the right, has lingered beyond the close of the window. If the Conceicao report is accurate, it reinforces the sense that Liverpool were willing to move decisively for a solution, but without landing one. That leaves the club facing familiar questions about recruitment clarity, role definition and whether the right-wing position was addressed with enough certainty when it mattered most. Our View From a Liverpool perspective, this is one of those reports that feels plausible enough to be uncomfortable. If the club really did put €50m on the table for Conceicao, then it suggests there was genuine anxiety late in the process. That does not automatically mean he is a poor player, far from it, but it does hint at a market where Liverpool were reacting rather than dictating. The biggest concern is the profile of the search. Supporters can accept missing out on elite targets because that happens to every club. What becomes harder to accept is a window where several names emerge, none arrives, and the underlying need still exists. That creates doubt over whether the recruitment team were fully aligned on the level required. There is also a broader issue around messaging. Liverpool are expected to plan ahead, especially in key attacking positions. If there was no settled right-wing solution ready to go, then fans are entitled to wonder why such an important area appeared to be left so open. At the same time, there is a case for caution before going too far. Plenty of reported bids look different once the full picture emerges. Yet if this account is close to the mark, supporters will see it as another sign that Liverpool entered a crucial market need without enough certainty, and paid the price for it.

item.title: Amorim to skip pre-match press conferences for Milan games against Atalanta and Udinese
item.description: Amorim to skip pre-match press conferences for Milan games against Atalanta and Udinese Ruben Amorim will not hold his usual pre-match press conference ahead of Milan’s Serie A clash with Atalanta at San Siro on Sunday. He will skip next Saturday’s briefing before the trip to Udinese too. According to MilanNews24 , there is nothing unusual behind the decision. The arrangement was planned well in advance with the club and is purely down to Milan’s packed schedule across Serie A and the Europa League. REGGIO NELL’EMILIA, ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Ruben Amorim Head Coach of AC Milan looks on during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and AC Milan at Mapei Stadium – Citta’ del Tricolore on October 11, 2026 in Reggio nell’Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) Milan boss Amorim prioritises Milanello work amid Europa League schedule Amorim already faced the media on Thursday night in Salzburg, after Milan’s Europa League fixture . The same will happen next week, when he speaks in Bournemouth following the third round of the league phase against the Cherries on 22 October. With those European commitments falling so close to the domestic fixtures, the Portuguese coach has chosen to use the extra time on the training pitch at Milanello rather than in front of the cameras. ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Ruben Amorim, Manager of AC Milan, looks on before the Serie A match between AC Milan and US Lecce at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 20, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Amorim, who is usually expansive on tactics and wider talking points in his pre-match briefings, will still speak to the media after both games, against Sarri’s Atalanta and in Udine.

item.title: What does a Tri-series mean in cricket? Format, rules, points system and how it works
item.description: What does a Tri-series mean in cricket? Format, rules, points system and how it works originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: A tri-series is a short event where three teams play each other and the top two reach the final. Points are usually two for a win and one for a tie or no result, and net run rate often separates teams that finish level. Afghanistan , Bangladesh and Zimbabwe begin a tri-series in the UAE on October 17, and Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka begin one in Pakistan on October 18. What is a tri-series in cricket? A tri-series is an international cricket series played among three teams. It is neither a two-team affair like the bilateral series nor a big tournament like the World Cup. It sits between the two. Three teams play each other in one short tournament, and the top two meet in a final to decide the winner. Tri-series are almost always played in either the ODI or T20I format. They are also called tri-nation or triangular series. Boards use them to give teams extra matches before major tournaments. The format has a long history. Australia held a tri-series every summer from 1979-80, and other countries have used the idea too. This month, two ODI tri-series begin in Asia, one in the UAE and one in Pakistan. Both finish before the end of October. MORE: GOAT in ODI cricket: Ranking the 10 greatest One Day International cricketers ever Tri-series: Rules, format and points system A tri-series has two stages. In the league stage, each team plays the other two. Some series play each pair once, while others play each pair twice. The top two teams after the league stage meet in the final, and the third team is out. Finals are usually a single match. Australia's old tri-series often used a best-of-three final instead, where the first side to win two matches took the trophy. A few years even used a best-of-five final. The rules can change from series to series. Points are simple in most series. In the 2014 Zimbabwe tri-series, a win earned two points, a tie or no result earned one point, and a loss earned none. Some series also add bonus points, so the exact rules can differ. MORE: Who will win the trophy if the series decider is washed out by rain? Points system in a tri-series Result Points Win 2 Tie 1 No result 1 Loss 0 Net run rate, or NRR, is used when teams are level. It is the runs a team scores per over, minus the runs it concedes per over, across the whole league stage. A team that is bowled out is treated as having faced its full quota of overs. item.content:encoded: What does a Tri-series mean in cricket? Format, rules, points system and how it works originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: A tri-series is a short event where three teams play each other and the top two reach the final. Points are usually two for a win and one for a tie or no result, and net run rate often separates teams that finish level. Afghanistan , Bangladesh and Zimbabwe begin a tri-series in the UAE on October 17, and Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka begin one in Pakistan on October 18. What is a tri-series in cricket? A tri-series is an international cricket series played among three teams. It is neither a two-team affair like the bilateral series nor a big tournament like the World Cup. It sits between the two. Three teams play each other in one short tournament, and the top two meet in a final to decide the winner. Tri-series are almost always played in either the ODI or T20I format. They are also called tri-nation or triangular series. Boards use them to give teams extra matches before major tournaments. The format has a long history. Australia held a tri-series every summer from 1979-80, and other countries have used the idea too. This month, two ODI tri-series begin in Asia, one in the UAE and one in Pakistan. Both finish before the end of October. MORE: GOAT in ODI cricket: Ranking the 10 greatest One Day International cricketers ever Tri-series: Rules, format and points system A tri-series has two stages. In the league stage, each team plays the other two. Some series play each pair once, while others play each pair twice. The top two teams after the league stage meet in the final, and the third team is out. Finals are usually a single match. Australia's old tri-series often used a best-of-three final instead, where the first side to win two matches took the trophy. A few years even used a best-of-five final. The rules can change from series to series. Points are simple in most series. In the 2014 Zimbabwe tri-series, a win earned two points, a tie or no result earned one point, and a loss earned none. Some series also add bonus points, so the exact rules can differ. MORE: Who will win the trophy if the series decider is washed out by rain? Points system in a tri-series Result Points Win 2 Tie 1 No result 1 Loss 0 Net run rate, or NRR, is used when teams are level. It is the runs a team scores per over, minus the runs it concedes per over, across the whole league stage. A team that is bowled out is treated as having faced its full quota of overs. What happens if teams finish level on points? If two teams are level, the series rules decide who goes through. In most cases, the first check is the number of wins. Next comes the wins against the other tied team, then bonus points, and finally NRR. A three-way tie is harder. Say each team wins two matches and loses two in a six-match series. All three finish on four points with the same number of wins, so NRR decides. The table below is only an example, and the team with the lowest NRR goes out. Example of a three-way tie on points Team Played Won Lost Points NRR Outcome Team A 4 2 2 4 +0.40 Reaches the final Team B 4 2 2 4 +0.15 Reaches the final Team C 4 2 2 4 -0.55 Out A washed-out match gives each team one point and no win. That can change a close race for second place. Some series also have rules for the final. A tied final can go to a Super Over, and the trophy can be shared if rain stops play. What if every league match is washed out? Each washed-out match gives both teams one point. If every league match in a tri-series is washed out, all three teams finish on the same points with no wins. NRR also stays at zero because matches with no result are left out of the calculation. The rules of past tri-series do not solve this. The 2014 Zimbabwe series went from wins to bonus points to NRR. The 2018 Trans-Tasman T20 series went from NRR to fours to sixes. With no balls bowled, all of those are zero, so the organisers could turn to ICC team rankings to decide the top two. MORE: Prediction: South Africa vs. Australia 2nd Test lineups and pitch report Famous tri-series in cricket history Tri-series have given cricket some of its best-known matches and rule changes. Some are remembered for one innings, others for a controversy or a famous chase. Here are seven that people still talk about, from Australia in 1979-80 to Pakistan in 2025. 1979-80 Benson & Hedges World Series Cup (Australia) – England beat the West Indies by two runs after captain Mike Brearley sent all his fielders to the boundary for the last ball. Fielding restrictions came in the next season. 1980-81 Benson & Hedges World Series Cup (Australia) - Trevor Chappell bowled the last ball underarm against New Zealand at the MCG on February 1, 1981, to stop a six that would have tied the game. The ICC banned underarm bowling afterwards. 1983-84 Benson & Hedges World Series Cup (Australia) - The second final between Australia and West Indies at the MCG ended level on 222 each, the first tied ODI. West Indies won the series. 1998 Coca-Cola Cup (Sharjah) - Sachin Tendulkar's Desert Storm 143 against Australia took India into the final, where he made 134 on his birthday and India won. 2002 NatWest Series (England) - India chased 326 against England in the final at Lord's, with Yuvraj Singh and Mohammad Kaif adding 121. Sourav Ganguly waved his shirt from the balcony after the win. 2007-08 Commonwealth Bank Series (Australia) - India beat Australia 2-0 in the best-of-three finals, with Tendulkar making 117 not out in the first at Sydney. It was India's only title in the Australian tri-series. 2025 Pakistan Tri-Nation Series - Pakistan chased 353 against South Africa, their highest successful ODI chase, with hundreds from Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha. New Zealand won the title by beating Pakistan in the final. Upcoming tri-series in 2026 Tri-series Teams Dates Afghanistan ODI tri-series (UAE) Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe October 17 to 23, 2026 Pakistan ODI tri-series (Pakistan) Pakistan, England, Sri Lanka October 18 to 31, 2026 To keep up to date with all the latest cricket news and share your opinion on the biggest topics, visit our Facebook , Instagram and X (Twitter) pages.

item.title: Broncos K Wil Lutz clarifies ‘shush’ celebration with message to Denver fans
item.description: Wil Lutz ended Thursday night’s game against the Seattle Seahawks with a 53-yard field goal in overtime, giving the Denver Broncos a 17-14 win at Empower Field at Mile High. His celebration drew nearly as much attention as the kick, because Lutz turned toward the home crowd with a gesture that looked like a shush. Denver led 14-3 entering the fourth quarter before Seattle tied it on Jason Myers’ 34-yard field goal with seven seconds left in regulation. Sam Darnold then threw an interception to Ja’Quan McMillian on the first possession of overtime, and the Broncos took over at Seattle’s 43-yard line before Lutz finished it. Jan 25, 2026; Denver, CO, USA; Denver Broncos place kicker Wil Lutz (3) prepares to kick a field goal against the New England Patriots during the first half in the 2026 AFC Championship Game at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images NFL aggregator Dov Kleiman claimed Lutz was facing “severe backlash” from Broncos fans, and plenty of fans answered that post by defending the kicker. Lutz went to X early Saturday to settle it himself. 𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚: Broncos kicker Wil Lutz is facing severe backlash from Denver fans after he did the shush celebration at home after his game-winning kick. We have never seen anything like this. https://t.co/ikBNchCErk — Dov Kleiman (@NFL_DovKleiman) October 16, 2026 To clarify any misunderstanding….We have the best fans and home field advantage in the NFL ,I’ll continue to voice that my entire time as a Bronco. The critics and all the noise we as a team, and personally, face can cause the emotion to come out sometimes. It’s such a cool moment to be able to hit big kick in that setting for this team, in front of our fans…it’s what we live for. I love the support of our fans and the standard you all hold us to, it’s why we want to win for this city and fan base! We all play with a chip on our shoulder, and I hope that makes everyone proud! Onward and upward! — Wil Lutz (@wil_lutz5) October 17, 2026 “To clarify any misunderstanding… We have the best fans and home field advantage in the NFL, I’ll continue to voice that my entire time as a Bronco. The critics and all the noise we as a team, and personally, face can cause the emotion to come out sometimes. It’s such a cool moment to be able to hit big kick in that setting for this team, in front of our fans… it’s what we live for. I love the support of our fans and the standard you all hold us to, it’s why we want to win for this city and fan base! We all play with a chip on our shoulder, and I hope that makes everyone proud! Onward and upward!” Lutz wrote. Why Lutz had critics to answer before Thursday’s kick Lutz entered Thursday having missed a field goal in each of Denver’s previous three games: a 43-yarder against the Rams, a 58-yarder against the 49ers and a 42-yarder in the fourth quarter of the Week 5 win over the Chargers. That left him 8 of 11 on the season, after he made more than 80% of his kicks last year. Nov 10, 2024

Nov 10, 2024; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Denver Broncos place kicker Wil Lutz (3) attempts a field goal with one second back that is blocked by Kansas City Chiefs defensive end Mike Danna (51) (not pictured) during the second half at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. We show up every day, we work, we try to figure out what’s going on, and at the end of the day it’s one kick at a time.” Lutz said. The 53-yarder was the 22nd game-winning kick of his career , the most in the league since he entered it as an undrafted free agent in 2016. “It’s hard to really explain the emotional side of it, the good and the bad. Like I said, I think anybody in my position, anybody on this team, lives for those moments. Glad we were able to put it through.” Lutz said. The make moved him to 9 of 12 this season. Denver, now 4-2, visits the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 25, and the Broncos return home Nov. 1 against the Kansas City Chiefs. item.description: Tennessee vs. Alabama radio coverage: Station, channel, streaming to listen live to college football game broadcast originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's the third Saturday in October, which means it's time for Tennessee vs. Alabama. The 14th-ranked Vols host the No. 6 Crimson Tide on Saturday in a key matchup for each team's College Football Playoff resume. Each has one blemish on its record in the form of a 20-17 home loss to one of the top two teams in the country at the time of the game — Tennessee falling to then-No. 1 Texas three weeks ago and Alabama to No. 2 Georgia last weekend. There's no shame in either of those defeats against elite opposition, but this is a critical bounceback opportunity for both. It should be a good one in Knoxville.
