item.title: Bruins' Comeback Win Creates Fascinating Question Before Kings Game
item.description: Bruins' Comeback Win Creates Fascinating Question Before Kings Game originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins could have walked away from Anaheim with plenty of excuses Friday night. They were playing on the road, surrendered two goals late in the opening period, and needed a comeback against a Ducks team that had seized the early momentum. Instead, the Bruins produced another victory, defeating Anaheim 4-2 and extending their winning streak to four games. David Pastrnak reached another impressive career milestone. Frederic Brunet scored his first NHL goal. Elias Lindholm delivered the winner, and Matthew Poitras provided insurance. But perhaps the most interesting part of the evening was what happened in Boston's net. Michael DiPietro earned his first NHL victory with 25 saves, giving the Bruins another encouraging development as they prepare for Saturday night's matchup against the Los Angeles Kings. Michael DiPietro Gives Bruins Something To Think About DiPietro was not handed an easy assignment. Anaheim generated opportunities early, and the Bruins allowed two goals in the final minute of the opening period. Suddenly, Boston needed its goaltender to prevent the game from getting away while the offense searched for answers. #NHLBruins WIN!!!! https://t.co/jZHrRmsEtd — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 17, 2026 DiPietro did exactly that. He stopped the Ducks from adding to their lead and gave Boston enough time to work its way back into the contest. The performance was not necessarily a statement that the Bruins should change their goaltending hierarchy. Jeremy Swayman remains an important part of the team's plans. However, DiPietro demonstrated something valuable. Boston can receive a competitive performance from another goaltender when circumstances require it. That matters during a long NHL season, particularly when a team is navigating consecutive games and extensive travel. A goaltender's first NHL victory is a personal milestone. For the organization, it can also provide an encouraging indication of its available depth. Young Bruins Continue Making An Impression Boston's comeback was not simply the result of its established stars taking over. Brunet scored his first NHL goal during the second period, cutting Anaheim's lead to 2-1 and giving the Bruins an important lift. James Hagens assisted on the goal and later helped set up Poitras' insurance tally. Those contributions are significant because the Bruins are trying to establish a winning identity while integrating younger players into meaningful situations. Veterans such as Pastrnak and Lindholm will continue carrying major responsibilities. That is expected. The more interesting question is whether Boston's younger contributors can consistently make a difference when games become uncomfortable. Friday provided an encouraging example. Brunet delivered a goal when the Bruins needed a response. Hagens contributed to multiple scoring

The Boston Bruins could have walked away from Anaheim with plenty of excuses Friday night. They were playing on the road, surrendered two goals late in the opening period, and needed a comeback against a Ducks team that had seized the early momentum. Instead, the Bruins produced another victory, defeating Anaheim 4-2 and extending their winning streak to four games. David Pastrnak reached another impressive career milestone. Frederic Brunet scored his first NHL goal. Elias Lindholm delivered the winner, and Matthew Poitras provided insurance. But perhaps the most interesting part of the evening was what happened in Boston's net. Michael DiPietro earned his first NHL victory with 25 saves, giving the Bruins another encouraging development as they prepare for Saturday night's matchup against the Los Angeles Kings. Michael DiPietro Gives Bruins Something To Think About DiPietro was not handed an easy assignment. Anaheim generated opportunities early, and the Bruins allowed two goals in the final minute of the opening period. Suddenly, Boston needed its goaltender to prevent the game from getting away while the offense searched for answers. #NHLBruins WIN!!!! https://t.co/jZHrRmsEtd — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 17, 2026 DiPietro did exactly that. He stopped the Ducks from adding to their lead and gave Boston enough time to work its way back into the contest. The performance was not necessarily a statement that the Bruins should change their goaltending hierarchy. Jeremy Swayman remains an important part of the team's plans. However, DiPietro demonstrated something valuable. Boston can receive a competitive performance from another goaltender when circumstances require it. That matters during a long NHL season, particularly when a team is navigating consecutive games and extensive travel. A goaltender's first NHL victory is a personal milestone. For the organization, it can also provide an encouraging indication of its available depth. Young Bruins Continue Making An Impression Boston's comeback was not simply the result of its established stars taking over. Brunet scored his first NHL goal during the second period, cutting Anaheim's lead to 2-1 and giving the Bruins an important lift. James Hagens assisted on the goal and later helped set up Poitras' insurance tally. Those contributions are significant because the Bruins are trying to establish a winning identity while integrating younger players into meaningful situations. Veterans such as Pastrnak and Lindholm will continue carrying major responsibilities. That is expected. The more interesting question is whether Boston's younger contributors can consistently make a difference when games become uncomfortable. Friday provided an encouraging example. Brunet delivered a goal when the Bruins needed a response. Hagens contributed to multiple scoring plays. Poitras helped put the game away. That is precisely the type of production that can make a team more difficult to defend over the course of a season. MORE : How to Watch Bruins vs. Kings Tonight: Channel, Live Stream & Start Time for NHL Game Another Challenge Arrives Immediately The Bruins will not have much time to celebrate. Boston faces Los Angeles on Saturday at 9 p.m. ET, completing a back-to-back set in Southern California. That quick turnaround creates decisions involving goaltending, lineup management and energy. It also presents a different kind of test. The Bruins have demonstrated that they can recover from an early deficit. Now they must show they can maintain their intensity with limited recovery time. Friday's victory improved Boston to 6-2-0, an encouraging opening to the season. Four consecutive wins have created momentum, but the schedule will continue testing the team's depth. The power play played a major role against Anaheim, accounting for three of Boston's four goals. The Bruins cannot assume that level of production will arrive every night. They will need contributions at even strength, reliable defensive play and goaltending capable of keeping them competitive. DiPietro provided the latest example of that final ingredient. For a team hoping to build something sustainable, that might be just as important as another spectacular goal from Pastrnak. The Bruins have their stars. Friday suggested they might also have some intriguing answers behind them. More Bruins Latest Bruins news TD Garden fan guide: What to know before you go Complete history of Bruins championships

item.title: Ladd McConkey Injury Update: Chargers WR’s Week 6 Status Revealed
item.description: Ladd McConkey has battled injuries throughout the 2026 season, but he appears to be ready to go for Week 6. Originally entering the league as a second-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft , the Georgia product took the league by storm and immediately established himself as one of Justin Herbert’s most reliable targets. Starting in 14 games while making 16 appearances, the wideout finished his inaugural campaign with 82 receptions for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns on 112 targets. While he wasn’t quite as effective in Year 2, he remained a key part of the offense. Now entering Week 6, Ladd McConkey has been one of the few consistent weapons in the Los Angeles Chargers offense, and he may finally be able to help the team earn its first win of the season. The third-year wideout does not have an injury designation on the team’s official report , so he should be ready to go for Sunday. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor Ladd McConkey Injury Update: Chargers WR Misses Practice The Last Word It’s hard to overstate just how important Ladd McConkey is for the Chargers to have any shot at pulling an upset against the Kansas City Chiefs. At 0-5, the Chargers playoff hopes are all but over, and they desperately need to defeat their division rival if they want to keep even the slightest chance of playoff hopes alive. It’s hard to call any game a “must-win” this early in the season, but that’s exactly what Week 6 is for the Los Angeles Chargers. At 0-5, the team is already 4.5 games behind the Kansas City Chiefs, and their Wild Card chances are pretty much gone. There is no precedent for an 0-6 team to make the playoffs, and Ladd McConkey is pretty much the only shot this team has of moving the football. Kansas City has one of the league’s best defenses, and the Chargers will need their top receiver to play his best football if they want to come out on top. Main Photo: William Laing – Imagn Images

item.title: Prep talk: Dave Yanai continues to love watching basketball at 83
item.description: Former Fremont High and Cal State Dominguez basketball coach Dave Yanai is 83. (Eric Sondheimer / Los Angeles Times) The Southern California college basketball kickoff luncheon was held on Wednesday at the Downtown Athletic Club, and sitting at one of the tables dressed in suit and tie was someone as knowledgeable as any coach in the room. Former Fremont High, Cal State Dominguez Hills and Cal State Los Angeles coach Dave Yanai, 83, was there. He won the John R. Wooden Award’s Legends of Coaching honor in 2021. He was inducted into the City Section Hall of Fame in 2023. Asked if he’s still watching basketball, Yanai said, “A lot.” He was the first Japanese American to be a head coach in college basketball. His nephew is Harvey Kitani, a future City Section Hall of Fame basketball coach who was at Fairfax and now Rolling Hills Prep. Yanai still has much to offer. You just have to ask. This is a daily look at the positive happenings in high school sports. To submit any news, please email eric.sondheimer@latimes.com. Sign up for the L.A. Times SoCal high school sports newsletter to get scores, stories and a behind-the-scenes look at what makes prep sports so popular. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

item.title: Former Barcelona director backs Deco’s work but warns of Real Betis’ star-studded squad: ‘A team to beat right now’
item.description: Former Barcelona director backs Deco’s work but warns of Real Betis’ star-studded squad: ‘A team to beat right now’ Former Barcelona sporting director Ramon Planes believes Hansi Flick’s side are currently the team to beat in Spanish football, but has warned that Real Betis possess the quality and confidence to make their meeting with the Catalans a compelling contest. Planes has a personal connection with both clubs, having worked at Barcelona before later taking Ez Abde to Betis. That experience gives his assessment of the upcoming encounter added significance, particularly with Manuel Pellegrini’s side enjoying an impressive spell and Barcelona looking to maintain their winning momentum. Speaking ahead of the meeting, Planes praised Betis’ development while reflecting on the time he spent at Barcelona and the progress both clubs have made. “They are two clubs that I really have a lot of esteem for. My time at Barça is something I’m proud of. “Today Betis is at its best, one of the best in its history and I think it comes from the idea of Angel Haro and Jose Miguel Lopez Catalan, at the time, to build a modern Betis,” said Planes. Planes identifies Betis as a serious Barcelona threat Planes believes Barcelona enter the fixture in stronger form, but insisted that Betis have the players and tactical confidence to challenge the reigning champions. The Andalusian club has developed into a team capable of competing with Spain’s leading sides, making this encounter a significant test for Flick. Ramon Planes has praised Deco’s work at Barcelona. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) “If anyone can give them a run for their money, it’s the current Betis side; they’re in excellent form and brimming with confidence. “They’re consistently putting in top-class performances; they proved that last season against the big teams. “They’ve got a ‘star-studded’ squad, full of top-quality players, and I think it’s going to be a cracking match because both teams pack a real punch.” Planes praises Deco’s Barcelona rebuild Planes also praised Barcelona’s recent performances and the work of current sporting director Deco. In particular, he pointed to the comeback against Galatasaray in Istanbul as evidence of the team’s confidence and ability to respond under pressure. “It’s clear that Barça are in good form. They proved it in the match against Galatasaray – such a difficult ground, and with the score at 1–0 down – the second half, when they came back with absolute confidence, was key. Planes has warned Barcelona about Real Betis’ level. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) “I think Barça’s transfer business has been very good and Deco is doing a fantastic job. He’s injected a lot of dynamism into the team and strengthened the squad. “That makes them the team to beat right now,” added Planes. item.title: ‘So rare’: Riley Gaines heaps huge praise on Sophie Cunningham for not issuing a ‘groveling apology’
item.description: Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images Former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines has nothing but praise for Sophie Cunningham. Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham is back in the news for another controversy during the offseason following an early playoff exit. This time, Cunningham had a short yet powerful message for the girls of Washington High School. The girls reportedly refused to play against a boy who was pretending to be a girl. Cunningham praised the girls, and her ‘good work’ message had former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines applauding the Fever guard’s actions. Madeline Carter/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images Riley Gaines commends Sophie Cunningham for standing her ground Over the past few months, Cunningham has been called out by several fans and analysts over her rigid stance on keeping biological men and boys out of women and girls’ sports. This dedication to her stance had Gaines impressed, as she had a solid message for the Fever guard’s ‘moral conviction.’ “Most people with large platforms cave and issue a groveling apology the minute they get a little pushback. Not Sophie Cunningham. Good for her. This type of moral conviction is so rare,” Gaines wrote on X . Even though Cunningham’s stance has led to many wanting the Fever to cut ties with her, she refuses to stand down. More importantly, as Gaines mentioned, Sophie is unapologetic about her actions as she believes in her viewpoint. Read more: Sophie Cunningham begs for ‘respect’ over Atlanta Dream’s WNBA Finals problem ‘One of us’ – Dan Dakich says Donald Trump has joined the Sophie Cunningham fan club ‘You can’t tackle’ – Sophie Cunningham expresses concern about Angel Reese’s physical playing style

item.title: Everton v Chelsea: Premier League – live
item.description: ⚽ Premier League updates from the 12.30pm BST kick-off ⚽ Live scoreboard | Tables | Top scorers | Email Scott Xabi Alonso speaks to TNT Sports. “We needed a win [against Bournemouth] but this was last week … one is not enough … we need to keep going, doing the right things, repeating and always improving game by game … [Reece James’ injury] makes it more limited but we have enough options … Romeo [Lavia] … [Valentin] Barco … they have played and now we have Mo [Caciedo] back and [Jordan Henderson] so we have more options … but for sure it’s a blow … we will need another big one in this stadium against Everton … tough opponent … they are in a good run so we are expecting a tough challenge.” Everton are currently in a good humour as well. Should they win this afternoon – and given how they’ve triumphed in this fixture in six of its last nine stagings, losing just the once, that’s very much a live prospect – they’ll move into fourth spot in the Premier League, for a couple of hours at least. Chelsea can do likewise. Continue reading...

item.title: NFL Trade Pitch Sees Seahawks Acquire Pro Bowl RB to Ignite Offense
item.description: CBS Sports's Jared Dubin proposed Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks acquire former Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty Veteran running back Tony Pollard could be on the move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty CBS Sports's Jared Dubin proposed Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks acquire former Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty The Seattle Seahawks are dealing with a turnover issue on offense. They have committed seven giveaways in their last two games, both of which were losses. But CBS Sports’s Jared Dubin doesn’t like what the Seahawks running game has shown either. For that reason, he proposed Seattle potentially change the Super Bowl race with a trade for Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. “The Seahawks cannot run the ball at all, as we have seen throughout this season and that was on full display on Thursday night against the Broncos,” wrote Dubin. “Pollard is no great shakes, but he’s got 1,000 yards in four consecutive seasons and is at least a professional runner who can get what’s blocked and a bit more. “The Seahawks should be getting Zach Charbonnet back fairly soon, but we don’t know if or when Jadarian Price will return. Pollard would be an upgrade over Emanuel Wilson and/or George Holani as a complement to Charbs. It’s not the sexiest deal in the world and might not even be the best possible use of resources, but the Seahawks do need help in the backfield.” Pollard has 273 rushing yards and a touchdown in five games for the Tennessee Titans this season. The veteran made the Pro Bowl with the Dallas Cowboys during his first 1,000-yard season in 2022. Seahawks Urged to Acquire Titans RB Tony Pollard Getty Veteran running back Tony Pollard could be on the move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. The Seahawks didn’t do that badly on the ground during Week 6 Seattle gained 113 rushing yards in Thursday’s contest versus the Denver Broncos . That production, though, came from a committee. Emanuel Wilson led the team with 52 rushing yards while George Holani and Velus Jones Jr. each had 20 rushing yards. Holani scored Seattle’s only rushing touchdown. Pollard would provide an upgrade over all three of those running backs. Last season, Pollard gained 1,082 yards on the ground with five touchdowns. It was his fourth straight 1,000-yard season. The running back has also registered at least 1,280 yards from scrimmage for four consecutive campaigns. With Pollard, the Seahawks could get back to their run-first mentality and take pressure away from quarterback Sam Darnold . The signal-caller has taken 10 sacks and thrown four interceptions in the past two losses. Getty The Seattle Seahawks are dealing with a turnover issue on offense. They have committed seven giveaways in their last two games, both of which were losses. But CBS Sports’s Jared Dubin doesn’t like what the Seahawks running game has shown either. For that reason, he proposed Seattle potentially change the Super Bowl race with a trade for Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. “The Seahawks cannot run the ball at all, as we have seen throughout this season and that was on full display on Thursday night against the Broncos,” wrote Dubin. “Pollard is no great shakes, but he’s got 1,000 yards in four consecutive seasons and is at least a professional runner who can get what’s blocked and a bit more. “The Seahawks should be getting Zach Charbonnet back fairly soon, but we don’t know if or when Jadarian Price will return. The veteran made the Pro Bowl with the Dallas Cowboys during his first 1,000-yard season in 2022. Seahawks Urged to Acquire Titans RB Tony Pollard Getty Veteran running back Tony Pollard could be on the move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. The Seahawks didn’t do that badly on the ground during Week 6 Seattle gained 113 rushing yards in Thursday’s contest versus the Denver Broncos . That production, though, came from a committee. Emanuel Wilson led the team with 52 rushing yards while George Holani and Velus Jones Jr. each had 20 rushing yards. Holani scored Seattle’s only rushing touchdown. Pollard would provide an upgrade over all three of those running backs. Last season, Pollard gained 1,082 yards on the ground with five touchdowns. It was his fourth straight 1,000-yard season. With Pollard, the Seahawks could get back to their run-first mentality and take pressure away from quarterback Sam Darnold . The signal-caller has taken 10 sacks and thrown four interceptions in the past two losses. Seahawks Running Back Depth After Week 6 Getty CBS Sports’s Jared Dubin proposed Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks acquire former Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Pollard could be a great upgrade for the Seahawks. But he could also still be an unnecessary addition. Before the regular season started, the hope in Seattle was the Seahawks could pair Zach Charbonnet with first-round rookie Jadarian Price this fall. Charbonnet hasn’t played yet this season while continuing to recovery from his January ACL injury. But head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters this past week the running back “looks tremendous.” Then on Friday, Macdonald described Price’s return to be happening “sooner-rather-than-later.” If those two are paired together on the field before the trade deadline on November 10, there would be little reason for the Seahawks to acquire Pollard. Having said that, Charbonnet is still only nine months removed from a serious knee injury. Price is also a rookie with three games of experience. At the very least, Pollard could provide backfield insurance in Seattle. But he also very well could be the boost the Seahawks offense really needs. item.title: NFL Network analyst floats surprising theory about Jalen Hurts’ absence from Eagles
item.description: Michael Robinson floated a theory about Jalen Hurts’ absence on NFL Network’s “NFL GameDay Kickoff” on Thursday, the same day the Philadelphia Eagles ruled their quarterback out of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers. Hurts has a superficial blood clot in his calf, and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, speaking on “The Pat McAfee Show,” described his status as out indefinitely. The Eagles are 2-3 after three straight losses, and Tanner McKee is expected to make the start against Carolina. Robinson, the former Seahawks fullback, opened by admitting he had no inside information and framed his argument as playing devil’s advocate. He pointed to the draft picks Philadelphia has collected in recent trades and said the organization appeared to be tying the outcome of this season to Hurts, which in his view would give the team a reason to move on from him later. He also noted that Hurts’ guaranteed money runs out after the 2027 season, even though his extension runs through 2028. Dec 14, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) on the filed after win against the Las Vegas Raiders at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images “If I’m Jalen Hurts, or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp, I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season… he’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” Robinson said. Philadelphia listed 24 players on its Thursday injury report. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with hamstring injuries, and guard Landon Dickerson has been on injured reserve with a knee bone bruise for all but one game this season . Robinson’s point about the injury list checks out against that report, and the motive he attached to Hurts is the part the team’s own account of the past two weeks actually contradicts. “if I’m Jalen Hurts − or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp − I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ “To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season..he’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” https://t.co/nqw8J8emov — Jon Marks (@JonMarksMedia) October 17, 2026 What the Eagles’ timeline shows about Hurts stepping away Hurts was cleated in the Oct. 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and asked for treatment on his calf on Oct. 8, according to the statement the Eagles released on Thursday . A precautionary ultrasound in London found the clot on Oct. 10, before the Jacksonville game. The medical staff and doctors in London cleared him, the league office was kept informed, and Hurts played the entire loss to the Jaguars without limitation. He practiced in full on Wednesday. A follow-up ultrasound later that night showed the small clot had moved, and the team ruled him out on Thursday. “Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course

Dec 14, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) on the filed after win against the Las Vegas Raiders at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images “If I’m Jalen Hurts, or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp, I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season… he’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” Robinson said. Philadelphia listed 24 players on its Thursday injury report. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with hamstring injuries, and guard Landon Dickerson has been on injured reserve with a knee bone bruise for all but one game this season . Robinson’s point about the injury list checks out against that report, and the motive he attached to Hurts is the part the team’s own account of the past two weeks actually contradicts. “if I’m Jalen Hurts − or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp − I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ “To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season..he’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” https://t.co/nqw8J8emov — Jon Marks (@JonMarksMedia) October 17, 2026 What the Eagles’ timeline shows about Hurts stepping away Hurts was cleated in the Oct. 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and asked for treatment on his calf on Oct. 8, according to the statement the Eagles released on Thursday . A precautionary ultrasound in London found the clot on Oct. 10, before the Jacksonville game. The medical staff and doctors in London cleared him, the league office was kept informed, and Hurts played the entire loss to the Jaguars without limitation. He practiced in full on Wednesday. A follow-up ultrasound later that night showed the small clot had moved, and the team ruled him out on Thursday. “Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment.” the Eagles said in the statement . Feb 2, 2026; San Francisco, CA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterrback Jalen Hurts (1) during NFC practice at the NFL Flag Fieldhouse at Moscone Center South Building. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Hurts knew about the clot before kickoff in London and played all four quarters anyway. The call to sit him came from a scan and the team’s doctors, after he had already been on the field for every one of the three straight losses Robinson suggests he is distancing himself from. The “lost season” in Robinson’s quote also belongs to a team that has played five of its 17 games. Robinson also said he was not dismissing how serious a superficial clot can be. The pushback came quickly anyway. Robert Griffin III wrote on X that the take was ridiculous and that the negative narratives around Hurts have to stop. The Eagles have not given a timetable for Hurts’ return. item.title: Patriots' Biggest Advantage Against Jets Might Not Be What Fans Expect
item.description: Patriots' Biggest Advantage Against Jets Might Not Be What Fans Expect originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots have spent much of the week answering questions about injured players, potential returns and how quickly their offense can get back to full strength. But heading into Sunday's AFC East matchup with the New York Jets, the biggest development might involve a player who will not be on the field. Jets running back Breece Hall has been ruled out of Sunday's game at Gillette Stadium. That creates an interesting opportunity for Mike Vrabel's defense, particularly with New England getting Christian Gonzalez back after the cornerback missed two consecutive games with a shoulder injury. The Patriots are 3-2 and riding a two-game winning streak. The Jets enter at 2-3, with several offensive injuries creating additional challenges for a team trying to establish consistency. For New England, the opportunity is obvious. The Patriots can make life considerably more difficult for the Jets by forcing their offense to operate without one of its most dangerous playmakers. Jets Lose An Important Offensive Weapon Hall's absence removes a player capable of changing a game without needing 20 or 25 touches. His ability to contribute as both a runner and receiver makes him particularly valuable to an offense that needs explosive plays. The Jets will turn to other options in their backfield, including Braelon Allen, who is coming off a strong performance against Cleveland. Allen rushed for a career-high 116 yards in that game, demonstrating that New York still has the personnel to establish a productive ground attack. TE Kenyon Sadiq and WR Omar Cooper Jr. are questionable for #NYJvsNE https://t.co/Zl9tJb1R7r — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 16, 2026 That means the Patriots cannot simply assume Hall's absence will eliminate the Jets' running game. However, the change could affect how New York approaches different situations. Hall's versatility presents challenges for linebackers and defensive backs, especially when he gets into space. Without him, the Jets may need to be more deliberate about creating favorable matchups. New York also ruled out wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and offensive lineman Dylan Parham, adding further complications to its offensive preparations. The Patriots should have opportunities to test those adjustments early. Christian Gonzalez Returns At An Important Time New England's secondary has its own injury problems. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis III and Karon Prunty have been ruled out, while Channing Canada is questionable with a hamstring injury. Those absences make Gonzalez's return especially important. Gonzalez practiced fully Friday and carries no game-day injury designation. That does not mean the Patriots have suddenly solved every problem in their secondary. It does mean they are getting back one of their most important defensive players at a time when they need stability

TE Kenyon Sadiq and WR Omar Cooper Jr. are questionable for #NYJvsNE https://t.co/Zl9tJb1R7r — New York Jets (@nyjets) October 16, 2026 That means the Patriots cannot simply assume Hall's absence will eliminate the Jets' running game. However, the change could affect how New York approaches different situations. Hall's versatility presents challenges for linebackers and defensive backs, especially when he gets into space. Without him, the Jets may need to be more deliberate about creating favorable matchups. New York also ruled out wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and offensive lineman Dylan Parham, adding further complications to its offensive preparations. The Patriots should have opportunities to test those adjustments early. Christian Gonzalez Returns At An Important Time New England's secondary has its own injury problems. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis III and Karon Prunty have been ruled out, while Channing Canada is questionable with a hamstring injury. Those absences make Gonzalez's return especially important. Gonzalez practiced fully Friday and carries no game-day injury designation. That does not mean the Patriots have suddenly solved every problem in their secondary. It does mean they are getting back one of their most important defensive players at a time when they need stability. The Jets still have Garrett Wilson, and rookie pass catchers Omar Cooper Jr. and Kenyon Sadiq are working toward returning to the lineup. That combination creates an interesting matchup. New York is missing important offensive pieces but could regain receiving options capable of testing New England's depth. Gonzalez gives the Patriots more flexibility in how they handle those challenges. MORE : 2-Time Super Bowl Champ Says Patriots Are NFL's Best Team Patriots Have A Chance To Control The Game Early The most important part of Sunday's matchup might be what happens before either team scores. If the Patriots consistently stop the run on early downs, they can force New York into longer passing situations. That would create opportunities for New England's pass rush and reduce the Jets' ability to dictate the pace. If Allen establishes himself early, however, the Jets could prevent New England from concentrating on the passing game. The Patriots also have decisions to make on offense. A.J. Brown remains questionable, and the team must decide whether to activate him from injured reserve before Saturday's deadline. But regardless of Brown's availability, New England has an opportunity to put pressure on the Jets by controlling the line of scrimmage. The Patriots do not need a spectacular defensive performance to take advantage of New York's injuries. They need discipline, sound tackling and an ability to prevent the Jets from finding easy yards. Sometimes the biggest advantage in a divisional game is not having the most exciting player on the field. It is making sure the other team cannot use its most exciting player against you. item.title: Cowboys’ Mike Pettine Sheds Light on His New Midseason Role
item.description: New Dallas Cowboys assistant Mike Pettine spoke out about his role with the team's coaching staff in front of reporters Friday. Getty New Dallas Cowboys assistant Mike Pettine spoke out about his role with the team's coaching staff in front of reporters Friday. Getty The Dallas Cowboys defense doesn’t look much different in 2026 than it did last season when it was one of the worst units in the league. But the Cowboys now hope an addition to the defensive staff could change that. Dallas added veteran NFL coach Mike Pettine to its defensive staff this week. Pettine will hold the title of senior defensive assistant. That’s not a particularly specific title. Pettine provided more details on his exact role to reporters Friday. “Just clearly support, just advise [Christian Parker],” Pettine said. “I think we’ll build a lot of the stuff together. We’ll game plan along with the staff. I just feel like my experience there, having gone against a lot of these opponents over time and kind of built books on most of these offensive coordinators, just feel I’ll be able to help that way. “Game day, I’ll just be up top as another set of eyes for him to bounces things off of, offer suggestions. I think the role will just kind of grow as it goes.” Pettine’s first NFL coaching role was with the Baltimore Ravens nearly 25 years ago. He coached under Rex Ryan for more than a decade, serving as defensive coordinator under Ryan with the New York Jets . Pettine was also Buffalo Bills defensive coordinator under Doug Marrone for a season. From 2014-15, Pettine served as head coach for the Cleveland Browns . “I think I can help a lot,” Pettine said. “It’s funny, I have a big four-inch thick book of what not to do, and a very thin one of what to do. So I think that’s key, is to be able to learn from others mistakes. “As much as you think you’re prepared for it, you’re really not until you get into it. And I think that’s where I’ll be able to help him.” Mike Pettine Speaks out on Cowboys Role Getty New Dallas Cowboys assistant Mike Pettine spoke out about his role with the team’s coaching staff in front of reporters Friday. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker appears to have a bright future in the league. The team’s brass, including owner Jerry Jones, still has a lot of confidence in Parker, who is in his first season as an NFL defensive coordinator. But Pettine has something Parker doesn’t — experience. A few years after his Browns head coaching tenure ended, he became a defensive coordinator again for three years with the Green Bay Packers . He was also an assistant head coach with the Minnesota Vikings from 2022-25. Pettine has previous experience with the Cowboys defensive coordinator as well. I think the role will just kind of grow as it goes.” Pettine’s first NFL coaching role was with the Baltimore Ravens nearly 25 years ago. So I think that’s key, is to be able to learn from others mistakes. “As much as you think you’re prepared for it, you’re really not until you get into it. And I think that’s where I’ll be able to help him.” Mike Pettine Speaks out on Cowboys Role Getty New Dallas Cowboys assistant Mike Pettine spoke out about his role with the team’s coaching staff in front of reporters Friday. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker appears to have a bright future in the league. He was also an assistant head coach with the Minnesota Vikings from 2022-25. Pettine has previous experience with the Cowboys defensive coordinator as well. Parker’s first NFL coaching job was under Pettine in 2019 with the Packers. Parker is the reason Pettine accepted the role in Dallas. On Friday, the senior assistant described Parker as a friend in need. That should make things easier for the Cowboys to navigate the potentially complicated matter of an assistant who just arrived with the team calling for changes. “CP knows me well enough that when I say something, some other people might be a bit shocked by it, and he just knows who I am,” Pettine said. “He’ll understand where I’m coming from. I’ll make some suggestions, and when we get behind closed doors, if I need to have some tough conversations, we’ll do it as I’ve always done with him or with other coaches. I don’t see that part of it being an issue.” Pettine suggested the Cowboys defense might need a lot of changes. But he stressed they won’t happen all at once and a majority of them will be minor but crucial changes. “One thing I learned a long time ago is football’s a game of a million little things,” Pettine said. “There’s no one magic play to run, it’s a lot of the detail stuff. Just been taking a lot of notes. It’s not like it’s something that, ‘Hey, we’re going to do these 30 things different today.’ “But it’s things that need to get addressed.” Pettine will coach his first game with the Cowboys in Week 6. Dallas will visit Green Bay on Sunday night. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Cowboys’ Mike Pettine Sheds Light on His New Midseason Role appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: “Never just for me”: Dossena carries girls’ dreams at U17 World Cup
item.description: “Never just for me”: Dossena carries girls’ dreams at U17 World Cup Before joining the Brazilian national team for the U-17 Women’s World Cup, goalkeeper Isadora Dassena had already made her mark in football. Finding the back of the net was how she first developed a trademark of her own. First with São Paulo. Then with Ferroviária, where she became the club’s first goalkeeper to score from a free kick in an official competition. Two clubs, two unprecedented achievements, and a trait that helps explain who this young player from Irati, Paraná, is: a willingness to go beyond what is expected of someone in her position. At six, Dossena chose to play in goal in outdoor football. But at nine, she decided to play outfield while remaining a goalkeeper in futsal. It was only at 12 that she committed to playing in goal outdoors, after a coach told her about potential that perhaps even she had not imagined. The decision paid off. At 14, Dossena joined São Paulo. The following year, she moved to Ferroviária, where she won the Brazilian U-17 Championship and continued building a career that now takes her to a new stage: the World Cup. Dossena during a Brazilian U-17 national team training session in Rabat, Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Brazilian National Team Her first call-up to the Brazilian national team late last year was a dream come true. For Dossena, wearing Brazil’s famous yellow shirt means much more than representing a badge. "Being part of everyday life with the national team is an enormous privilege. Both the coaching staff and the players try to keep the atmosphere as relaxed as possible so we can perform at our best," she says. In Morocco, where she is experiencing her first World Cup, the goalkeeper has also discovered football’s reach beyond the pitch. Amid different cultures, languages and customs, she stresses the value of belonging to a group working toward the same goal. "Our national team has a very relaxed atmosphere, while other teams tend to be more reserved. It’s really interesting to experience everything the World Cup has to offer," she says. Isadora Dossena preparing for the U-17 World Cup opener in Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Making history means paving the way While Dossena has already learned to surprise people on the pitch, off it she has discovered that her achievements can reach places in ways only football can inspire. She recently returned to Irati, the city in Paraná where she began playing alongside boys, to visit a girls’ football program. item.content:encoded: “Never just for me”: Dossena carries girls’ dreams at U17 World Cup Before joining the Brazilian national team for the U-17 Women’s World Cup, goalkeeper Isadora Dassena had already made her mark in football. Finding the back of the net was how she first developed a trademark of her own. First with São Paulo. Then with Ferroviária, where she became the club’s first goalkeeper to score from a free kick in an official competition. Two clubs, two unprecedented achievements, and a trait that helps explain who this young player from Irati, Paraná, is: a willingness to go beyond what is expected of someone in her position. At six, Dossena chose to play in goal in outdoor football. But at nine, she decided to play outfield while remaining a goalkeeper in futsal. It was only at 12 that she committed to playing in goal outdoors, after a coach told her about potential that perhaps even she had not imagined. The decision paid off. At 14, Dossena joined São Paulo. The following year, she moved to Ferroviária, where she won the Brazilian U-17 Championship and continued building a career that now takes her to a new stage: the World Cup. Dossena during a Brazilian U-17 national team training session in Rabat, Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Brazilian National Team Her first call-up to the Brazilian national team late last year was a dream come true. For Dossena, wearing Brazil’s famous yellow shirt means much more than representing a badge. "Being part of everyday life with the national team is an enormous privilege. Both the coaching staff and the players try to keep the atmosphere as relaxed as possible so we can perform at our best," she says. In Morocco, where she is experiencing her first World Cup, the goalkeeper has also discovered football’s reach beyond the pitch. Amid different cultures, languages and customs, she stresses the value of belonging to a group working toward the same goal. "Our national team has a very relaxed atmosphere, while other teams tend to be more reserved. It’s really interesting to experience everything the World Cup has to offer," she says. Isadora Dossena preparing for the U-17 World Cup opener in Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Making history means paving the way While Dossena has already learned to surprise people on the pitch, off it she has discovered that her achievements can reach places in ways only football can inspire. She recently returned to Irati, the city in Paraná where she began playing alongside boys, to visit a girls’ football program. Standing before girls who dream of becoming players, she showed them her Brazilian U-17 Championship medal and realized that her own journey is already inspiring others. “I was the only girl who played in my hometown, which is small, with around 60,000 people. I played with the boys. Recently, I went back and was so happy to see that they had set up programs. I visited one of them, and there were lots of girls, all happy. It’s really nice to see younger generations believing it’s possible, especially in a small town that gets little attention," she says. "It warms my heart because we realize that all the effort is paying off both on and off the pitch. Knowing that I’m an inspiration to other people is a huge motivation, because it will never be just about me," she adds. Those words take on even greater meaning when the goalkeeper talks about the national team. Facing Canada in their World Cup opener, Brazil will take on a tough opponent and have the chance to start forging their path in the tournament. Dossena knows they will need to give their all in every respect, but she is confident in the work the group has done. "What motivates us most is knowing that we’ll give everything we have, regardless of the level or who our opponents are. We’ll represent Brazil on the pitch. We don’t just play for those who are here, but also for everyone who was part of our preparations, for the fans, our families and the coaching staff, who can’t be out on the pitch but help us all the time. We’re very focused on this opening match. We’ll give everything we can. We’ll do what’s possible, and what seems impossible too," she says. Brazil’s U-17 women’s national team kicks off its World Cup campaign this Sunday (18) at noon (Brasília time). Brazil faces Canada at the Women’s Football Complex in Salé, Morocco. The Group C opener will be broadcast live on Sportv and streamed on FIFA+ and CAZÉTV. U-17 Women’s World Cup (Group C) Brazil vs. Canada DATE: Sunday, October 18 TIME: Noon (Brasília time) VENUE: Women’s Football Complex, Salé, Morocco WHERE TO WATCH: Sportv and streaming on FIFA+ and CAZÉTV This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Ex-Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. Has New Injury With Cowboys
item.description: Former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is back on the injury report ahead of Week 6. Getty Former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is back on the injury report ahead of Week 6. Getty Dallas Cowboys' Stephen Jones addressed new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. ahead of Week 6. Getty There’s a problem when one becomes the boy who cried wolf — no one believes you anymore. That’s an issue former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. seems to be experiencing early in his tenure with the Dallas Cowboys. Porter missed Week 5 with the stomach flu. Now entering Week 6, the Cowboys have Porter listed as questionable because of an ankle injury. The ankle ailment is a new development that some members of the Cowboys organization don’t appear to be acknowledging. But nonetheless, Porter was limited in practice Wednesday and Friday this week. This is notable because of the phantom back injury he had at the end of his Steelers tenure. Porter landed on the PUP list in late July because of his back. Then when the team failed to sign him to a contract extension, Porter continued to miss time because of his back problem. The cornerback sat out three games and was set to miss Week 4 before the Steelers traded him to Dallas. Porter made his Cowboys debut four days after the trade. But he missed the following game and is in danger of sitting out Sunday. Will Joey Porter Jr. Miss Cowboys Matchup vs. Packers? Getty Former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is back on the injury report ahead of Week 6. The Cowboys have made clear that the cornerback isn’t going to get a new contract before the offseason. That was an issue with the Steelers when the team ended negotiations when the regular season began. However, Porter explained to reporters upon arriving in Dallas he didn’t feel valued in Pittsburgh. Since no contract negotiations have taken place in Dallas, it’s unlikely the Cowboys have made him feel disrespected. Put sanother way, it doesn’t make much sense Porter would play four days after getting traded to Dallas and then resume his hold-in. If the contract was an issue, then Porter wouldn’t have played in Week 4 for Dallas. The cornerback only missed Week 5 because he came down with a terrible flu hours before the game. “I really just couldn’t hold anything down,” he told DallasCowboys.com . “You know, I just kept throwing up. I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn’t hold in deep down. “So that’s when they made the call to send me home.” Porter then told DallasCowboys.com’s Patrik Walker that he hoped to not be on a snap count this Sunday. It’s notable, though, that Walker reported Porter returned healthy and practiced Wednesday when he actually was limited. Porter was limited hours prior to Walker publishing his story covering Porter’s sudden Week 5 illness. The cornerback probably deserves the benefit of the doubt. But it’s also understandable if Steelers f

I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn’t hold in deep down. “So that’s when they made the call to send me home.” Porter then told DallasCowboys.com’s Patrik Walker that he hoped to not be on a snap count this Sunday. It’s notable, though, that Walker reported Porter returned healthy and practiced Wednesday when he actually was limited. Porter was limited hours prior to Walker publishing his story covering Porter’s sudden Week 5 illness. The cornerback probably deserves the benefit of the doubt. But it’s also understandable if Steelers fans and others don’t want to give it to him. Stephen Jones Speaks out on Porter Getty Dallas Cowboys’ Stephen Jones addressed new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. ahead of Week 6. NFL fans will find out for certain whether Porter is sincere that he wants to move forward with the Cowboys this season on Sunday night. Stephen Jones, though, did his best to squash any concern during his radio appearance Friday. “Oh, absolutely. I think he’s all in,” said Jones, via The Athletic’s Jon Machota . “He wants to be out there; he was sick. He couldn’t play last week with the flu. But he obviously played in our first game, and I think he’s fired up about what he can do to help us win against the Packers . Like Walker, Jones didn’t acknowledge Porter’s new ankle issue. Porter didn’t register a statistic in his Cowboys debut, but he scored strong analytical grades. Porter played 25 defensive snaps versus the Houston Texans . This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Ex-Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. Has New Injury With Cowboys appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘It’s an Indictment Against You’ — Stephen A. Smith Rips Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer Over Reaction to Player-Only Meeting
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a disappointing loss against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. The team’s defense was seen struggling throughout the game. The organization’s head coach, Brian Schottenheimer, has been facing criticism as he was seen praising the players for holding a players-only meeting to address their defensive struggles. Jun 5, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; Stephen A. Smith looks on before the game between the San Antonio Spurs and the New York Knicks in game two of the 2026 NBA Finals at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Stephen A. Smith Slams Cowboys Coach Over Meeting In a recent episode of ESPN’s “First Take”, ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith shared a very different view of what a players-only meeting tells him and said “It means the coach ain’t reaching you. So when I see a head coach, and he’s applauding the players only meeting, my attitude with him, ‘How are you okay with that?’ If you’re okay with that, you can point to players being accountable, and taking ownership, and all of those cliché kinds of things we may have heard, but ultimately it’s an indictment against you because it’s your job to reach them.” “You ain’t playing. What the hell are you doing?” Smith added. “If they got to reach themselves, if they got to rally amongst themselves, if they’ve got to something or gumption up whatever it is necessary to right the ship that is clearly wrong, then why aren’t you the person facilitating that? If you’re not the person facilitating that, why the hell are you the coach? That’s to me is what the problem was.” The controversy came to light when linebacker DeMarvion Overshown revealed that players had gathered without the coaching staff to discuss their performance and evaluate whether they were meeting the standards expected of the team. The organization’s recent performance has raised questions about the team’s defensive struggles. The franchise was not able to deliver its best performance and was seen struggling throughout the game, thus showing a lack of tackling, consistency, and the ability to limit opponents’ production, despite making personnel changes intended to strengthen the unit. It would be interesting to see whether Brian Schottenheimer will be able to address the team’s defensive struggles and help the organization get back on track. The head coach will need to find ways to improve communication, strengthen the team’s defensive strategy, and ensure that players are held accountable for their performances. The upcoming games will be crucial for the Cowboys as they look to overcome their recent setbacks. Schottenheimer will have to prove that he can lead the team through difficult situations and help the players deliver better performances on the field. item.title: ‘He’s the Next Man Up’ — Mary Kay Cabot Denies Rumored Shedeur Sanders Trade After Browns QB Hired an Agent
item.description: Cleveland Browns’ backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders has once again caught fans’ attention as the quarterback hired an agent for the first time since joining the league. The step taken by Sanders does not come as a shock, as after losing the QB1 battle to Deshaun Watson ahead of the 2026 season, fans and analysts began speculating about a potential trade to another team. Oct 1, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) and quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) before the game at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Mary Kay Cabot Dismisses Shedeur Sanders Trade Rumors In a recent episode of “92.3 The Fan”, Browns insider Mary Kay Cabot was seen talking about the young quarterback, explaining that the organization views him as an important part of its future, and said: “ Well, I think if you look back to the whole draft process, he did not have an agent. He did not have guidance in a professional manner in terms of being signed with an agency. And some people that I’ve talked to in the league think that hurt him in the process, just in some of his decisions about which visits he wanted to take or how he wanted to approach some of those interviews. And so I think this is just part of the process as you go through your NFL career and you try to navigate your situation. It’s probably a good idea for him to have some type of representation. And I know within the last six months, he’s also hired a marketing agency. “ “So I think he’s just taking charge of his career in ways that he might not have really known as much about when he was just coming out of school. I don’t know if that is the motive here or that is part of the agenda. I don’t have any idea. We haven’t really talked to Shador very much. He’s not in the locker room. And there really, you know, there really isn’t much reason to talk to the backup quarterback at this time of year when he’s not playing. So we haven’t talked to him about this yet. And I don’t know if there’s any type of, like I said, any type of an agenda here. But I know that the Browns don’t want to trade him. He’s next in line. He’s next man up. And they always need at least two quarterbacks a year. So I don’t know that you would want to go and ask for a trade when you’re one play away from getting in the game for the Cleveland Browns.” “I know that the Browns don’t want to trade him. item.title: ‘I Do Believe in Keelon Russell’ — Analyst Shows Faith in Alabama Star QB After Loss Against Georgia
item.description: The Alabama Crimson Tide suffered a disappointing 20-17 loss against Georgia. Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell put in an impressive performance and gave his best despite the setbacks he experienced against Georgia. College football analyst Joel Klatt believes that one difficult performance should not overshadow Russell’s overall potential or the progress he has made during his first season as Alabama’s starting quarterback. July 30, 2025; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Quarterback Keelon Russell throws during the first practice session of the preseason for the Alabama Crimson Tide. Joel Klatt Expresses Thoughts On Keelon Russel; and Alabama In a recent episode of “The Joel Klatt Show”, the analyst shared his views on the young quarterback and said: “I do believe in Keelon Russell, guys. Um, it wasn’t perfect, and there were certainly things that he was going to want back off of last week’s game, but trust me when I tell you this: I watched the entire film. It is very difficult to decipher Georgia’s defense.” “They hold their water, meaning that they disguise. They don’t tell you what you’re in pre-snap. You’ve got to decipher that post-snap. Very difficult for a young quarterback. He made some plays with his legs that are still, like, get-out-of-your-seat-style plays. This guy is a special player, folks. He really is. I like their defense. I thought that they ran it a lot better against Georgia than I anticipated, a lot better than they did a year ago.” Although the organization suffered a defeat, the performance given by the young quarterback will help identify areas for improvement as he continues developing at the college level. The young quarterback accepted his mistakes after the game, as he understood that missed throws had affected Alabama’s offensive execution. The young quarterback has shown remarkable positivity, as it is never easy to acknowledge your weaknesses and embrace them as opportunities for growth. With pressure on the field higher than ever, how a young quarterback responds to setbacks and carries himself through difficult moments can shape how an organization views his development and leadership. Alabama should take time to analyze its performance against Georgia and identify the areas that need improvement. The coaching staff can use the lessons from the Georgia game to help Russell recognize defensive schemes more quickly and make better decisions under pressure. Facing experienced defenses can be challenging for a young quarterback, but these experiences can also accelerate his development. If Russell continues to build confidence, improve his timing with receivers, and learn from his mistakes, he could become a more reliable leader for the Crimson Tide. The quarterback has given the organization a reason to believe in him, as he looks like someone who will continue to improve with time. His talent, determination, and ability to make difficult plays show that he has the potential to become a key player for Alabama. With Pressure

item.title: Max Verstappen unveils special Texas-themed helmet for F1 United States GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has revealed a special helmet for the United States Grand Prix, giving his usual design an Austin, Texas, makeover ahead of the race at the Circuit of the Americas. The Dutchman unveiled the new design on social media. "Texas bound. I’ll be coming to Austin with this special helmet!" he posted alongside detailed photos of the new helmet. The main change is to the lion on the top of the helmet, which now wears a cowboy hat. The lion stands out in blue on a white background and the red, white and blue theme has been retained throughout the whole helmet. At the time of writing, Verstappen's post had already received more than 747,000 likes. "10s across the board - the lion with the cowboy hat is incredible," one fan commented, while another added: "The lion in the cowboy hat is brilliant haha." Further reactions included: "Oh this is gorgeous", and "Simply lovely that helmet." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Max Verstappen (@maxverstappen1) To complement the new helmet, Verstappen and his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar will also be wearing special all-white, vintage-style race suits. The new designs have sparked hope among fans that the Milton Keynes outfit could introduce an all-white livery for the race in Austin, but this is yet to be confirmed. Read Also: Red Bull reveals striking white F1 race suits for US GP as fans call for matching livery Verstappen heads to Austin after back-to-back wins at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and the Singapore Grand Prix. He currently sits fourth in the drivers' standings with 221 points, 119 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli. But while most drivers have a weekend off from racing after an intense triple-header, Verstappen is racing in the GT World Challenge Europe finale at Portimao this weekend in the Verstappen Racing #3 Mercedes-AMG with Chris Lulham and Ben Barnicoat. The United States Grand Prix takes place at the Circuit of the Americas from 23-25 October and kicks off the next triple-header in the championship, with the Mexican and Brazilian Grands Prix in the two weeks following. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed
item.description: Jeremiyah Love has battled an ankle injury throughout the season, and the ailment will keep the running back sidelined for Week 6. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it’s easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson and Detroit’s Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport revealed the running back will not play in Week 6, as the team is resting him in hopes of ensuring his long-term health. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB OUT For Week 6 While Jeremiyah Love has played in every game this season, he hasn’t lived up to his pre-draft hype. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven’t done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn’t looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his previous form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier will get the start. The former Atlanta Falcon has had similar struggles behind Arizona’s offensive line, recording just 119 yards and one touchdown on 35 attempts throughout the young season. Main Photo: David Brytus – Imagn Images

item.title: Gervon Dexter Found His Fit in Atlanta. Did the Bears Miss the Signs?
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Gervon Dexter Sr. #95 of the Atlanta Falcons tackles Justice Hill #43 of the Baltimore Ravens in the second quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 24: General Manager Ian Cunningham of the Atlanta Falcons speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears are about to face a player who might make them question what they missed in him. Gervon Dexter Sr. was a second-round pick, a starting defensive tackle and a productive member of Chicago’s defensive line. Then, on August 30, the Bears traded him to Atlanta for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick. One month later, the Falcons handed Dexter a four-year contract extension worth $78 million, including $46.5 million guaranteed. Now, as the Bears prepare for Sunday’s matchup, Dexter arrives with something more interesting than a revenge narrative: evidence that a change of scenery can transform a player’s value. Atlanta didn’t just acquire Dexter. It appears to have unlocked him. What Changed for Gervon Dexter in Atlanta’s Defense? The numbers are difficult to ignore. Through five games of the 2026 season, Pro Football Focus has Dexter graded fourth among 133 interior defensive linemen, with 18 quarterback pressures and an 81.9 overall grade as of October 15. His pass-rush grade ranked seventh. Those are impressive results for a player who had barely been in Atlanta long enough to unpack. There is a tactical explanation worth exploring. Under defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, Atlanta has generated pressure without routinely sending extra defenders. Through its first three games, the Falcons recorded a 41.6% quarterback pressure rate while blitzing fewer than 20% of the time. Dexter produced 15 pressures during that opening stretch alone. That matters because pressure isn’t just about sacks. An interior defender who collapses the pocket can disrupt a quarterback’s timing, force hurried decisions and create opportunities for teammates. Dexter has the size and power to make life uncomfortable for offensive linemen, and Atlanta’s aggressive four-man rush appears to be giving him room to attack. Chicago’s Dennis Allen had a different defensive system, but it would be unfair to conclude that Allen simply didn’t know how to use him. Dexter was already a starter in Chicago, starting all 32 games across the 2024 and 2025 seasons and finishing second on the team in sacks in both years. The more revealing possibility is that Atlanta found a way to maximize qualities the Bears already knew he possessed. Sometimes it’s not simply about a player’s talent. It’s about the situation that makes better use of it. Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – FEBRUARY 24: General Manager Ian Cunningham of the Atlanta Falcons s
item.content:encoded: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Gervon Dexter Sr. #95 of the Atlanta Falcons tackles Justice Hill #43 of the Baltimore Ravens in the second quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 24: General Manager Ian Cunningham of the Atlanta Falcons speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears are about to face a player who might make them question what they missed in him. Gervon Dexter Sr. was a second-round pick, a starting defensive tackle and a productive member of Chicago’s defensive line. Then, on August 30, the Bears traded him to Atlanta for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick. One month later, the Falcons handed Dexter a four-year contract extension worth $78 million, including $46.5 million guaranteed. Now, as the Bears prepare for Sunday’s matchup, Dexter arrives with something more interesting than a revenge narrative: evidence that a change of scenery can transform a player’s value. Atlanta didn’t just acquire Dexter. It appears to have unlocked him. What Changed for Gervon Dexter in Atlanta’s Defense? The numbers are difficult to ignore. Through five games of the 2026 season, Pro Football Focus has Dexter graded fourth among 133 interior defensive linemen, with 18 quarterback pressures and an 81.9 overall grade as of October 15. His pass-rush grade ranked seventh. Those are impressive results for a player who had barely been in Atlanta long enough to unpack. There is a tactical explanation worth exploring. Under defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, Atlanta has generated pressure without routinely sending extra defenders. Through its first three games, the Falcons recorded a 41.6% quarterback pressure rate while blitzing fewer than 20% of the time. Dexter produced 15 pressures during that opening stretch alone. That matters because pressure isn’t just about sacks. An interior defender who collapses the pocket can disrupt a quarterback’s timing, force hurried decisions and create opportunities for teammates. Dexter has the size and power to make life uncomfortable for offensive linemen, and Atlanta’s aggressive four-man rush appears to be giving him room to attack. Chicago’s Dennis Allen had a different defensive system, but it would be unfair to conclude that Allen simply didn’t know how to use him. Dexter was already a starter in Chicago, starting all 32 games across the 2024 and 2025 seasons and finishing second on the team in sacks in both years. The more revealing possibility is that Atlanta found a way to maximize qualities the Bears already knew he possessed. Sometimes it’s not simply about a player’s talent. It’s about the situation that makes better use of it. Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – FEBRUARY 24: General Manager Ian Cunningham of the Atlanta Falcons speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) The Ian Cunningham Connection Makes This More Than a Fresh Start The man who brought Dexter to Atlanta knew him before the trade ever happened. Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham was Chicago’s assistant general manager when the Bears selected Dexter 53rd overall in 2023. He had a firsthand look at the defensive tackle’s development, his strengths and the limitations that may have influenced Chicago’s roster decisions. That background makes the speed of Atlanta’s commitment particularly striking. The Falcons didn’t wait half a season to decide whether Dexter was worth keeping. After three games, they were prepared to invest $78 million in his future. Cunningham praised Dexter’s power and disruptive ability when announcing the extension, describing him as a young, ascending talent. The commitment also suggests Atlanta believes his early production is sustainable, rather than a brief hot streak. Bears coach Ben Johnson has offered a more diplomatic assessment. As reported by Sports Illustrated , Johnson called Dexter a “phenomenal football player” and described the trade as a win-win, pointing to the fresh start and a defensive scheme that matches his skill set. That’s an important distinction. Chicago had reasons to make the move, including its plans for the defensive-line rotation and its desire to add depth in the secondary. The Bears weren’t necessarily declaring Dexter a bad player. They were deciding he wasn’t the right fit for their plans. Still, there is a difference between believing a player can succeed elsewhere and watching another organization immediately commit major money to him. Atlanta’s decision raises a legitimate question about whether Chicago fully appreciated Dexter’s abilities. Will Sunday’s Game Could Expose the Cost Dexter now gets to test his former team on the field. For Chicago’s offensive line, the challenge is straightforward: contain an interior defender who has become one of the league’s more productive early-season pass rushers. Dexter knows the Bears’ personnel, while Chicago knows his tendencies. Neither side will have the luxury of treating this as an ordinary matchup. The Bears also have their own defensive concerns, including Montez Sweat’s two-game suspension and Dayo Odeyingbo’s injury. But Dexter’s departure is a separate issue, and the value of the trade won’t be decided by one afternoon in Atlanta. The Bears received Phillips and a future draft pick. The Falcons received a starting-caliber defensive tackle and quickly secured his future. Both sides may ultimately benefit, but the early returns are undeniably favorable to Atlanta. Dexter doesn’t need to celebrate a sack or deliver a pointed message to his former team to make a statement. If he continues to disrupt Chicago’s offense, the performance will speak for itself. The bigger lesson for the Bears may be uncomfortable: sometimes a team correctly identifies a player’s talent but fails to find the best way to use it. Atlanta appears to have found that way with Dexter. Sunday’s game won’t settle the argument, but it could offer Chicago a glimpse of what it gave up. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Gervon Dexter Found His Fit in Atlanta. Did the Bears Miss the Signs? appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: The Florian Wirtz mystery: why has he not found Leverkusen form at Liverpool?
item.description: Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produce Some criticism has been OTT and a fee rising to £116m heightens demands but, yes, compared with his performances in Germany and for Germany Wirtz has underwhelmed at Liverpool. The past week has encapsulated his Liverpool career so far. In the Champions League rout of Lask he was everywhere, exploiting gaps between and behind the Austrian club’s defence and knitting together a dominant display against limited opposition. In the previous game against Manchester City , however, when Andoni Iraola needed big players to step up in the absence of Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, Wirtz was ineffective, wasteful and withdrawn when his team were chasing the game at 0-1. It also did not help his cause that Rayan Cherki, a cheaper alternative whom Liverpool considered and passed on, completed City’s victory with a sublime goal. AH Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.description: Spanish head coach will be under huge pressure if he comes unstuck again at home to Hull on Saturday Fulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions. Silva’s substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points. But Silva left last summer, joining Benfica after concluding he could achieve nothing more at Craven Cottage, and his replacement is already under pressure after some puzzling tactical choices.
